PAGES.title: Immunotherapy resistance evidence and treatment implications
blocks: Alexander Young | Metastatic microsatellite-stable rectal cancer | 18 November 2026 | Executive summary

Archival data support poor immune recruitment and a matrix-rich treated resection; the dominant current barrier remains unknown. My proposal through Dr Kesari/Asthra combines peptide vaccination, vactosertib, N-803 and checkpoint blockade. Vaccine priming and natural tumour antigen display are separate requirements; CD4/CD8 quality, co-delivery and entry still matter. The full regimen is unvalidated. Our 28-sample trial analysis found no significant association for four TGF-beta/fibroblast programmes (all q=.521). SMAD4 G359E has functional impairment evidence, with classification as a variant of uncertain significance retained. [VE1] [VE9] [VR1] [SM14]
Counterevidence and what can be inferred
Caris/Tempus CXCL9/10/11 below external-reference first quartile; BostonGene CXCL10 3rd percentile and immune non-inflamed portrait.
Few recruitment signals can be cause or consequence of weak local immunity. CD8A 56th percentile and historical liver T/NK cells argue against complete immune absence.
Vaccine/N-803 address priming/expansion; improved chemotaxis is conditional. More blood lymphocytes does not prove tumour entry.
Tempus matrix RNA; BostonGene CXCL12 99th; B7 fibroblast proteins plus THBS2 and ITGA5.
Caris FN1 4th percentile; repair/muscle admixture; no spatial barrier. The SMAD4 result supports functional impairment, but does not establish current-lesion loss or TGF-beta-driven ERK activation.
TGF-beta/CXCL12 combinations remain investigational. Trial RNA does not validate high stromal expression as a vactosertib selector; SMAD4/ERK findings do not establish sensitivity.
CD39/CD73/ENPP1 proteins and supporting resection RNA.
Enzyme presence does not establish metabolite flux or drug dependence.
Human CRC evidence supports trial discussion; no case-specific probability of benefit follows from expression.
BostonGene IRF1/TAP1/HLA low; APC/PTEN alterations; PTPN1/2 proteins present.
Caris IRF1/TAP1/HLA-A/B near median; bulk antigen-display proteins retained. No validated irreversible B2M loss.
DC vaccine presentation and cancer-cell peptide-HLA display must both work. Improved priming cannot bypass absent tumour targets.
AXL/MERTK/CSF1 RNA; macrophage proteins; THBS2/SPP1 connect stroma to recruitment.
Cell source and suppressive function unresolved. These signals overlap other axes.
Selective myeloid approaches have limited CRC efficacy; expression does not justify indiscriminate depletion.
MSS/low TMB; mixed DC markers; low recent lymphocytes. Intended Hiltonol and 19/20 manufactured targets are reported.
No measured tumour-reactive clone deficit or global DC absence. Final product release, balanced CD4/CD8 responses and current target display remain unconfirmed.
Vaccine/N-803 is plausible. FLT3L, CD40 and local priming are research leads; metabolic approaches rank lower. No validated response predictor.
COX2/PGE2, vascular/hypoxia and alternative checkpoints provide leads.
No dominant functional dependency; several markers and clinical studies are negative.
Lower-priority immune combinations; established CRC treatment evidence should carry greater weight.

Ranks are research priorities, not response predictions. CAF = cancer-associated fibroblast; DC = dendritic cell. N-803/Anktiva supports IL15 signalling; systemic CRC use is investigational. Pembrolizumab was discussed; BOT/BAL (botensilimab/balstilimab) is an alternative requiring renewed approval after prior progression. [VE9] [NV11]

PAGES.title: Ranking the resistance hypotheses
blocks: The nine hypotheses separate recruitment from priming and expansion. They are not independent: a shortage of tumour-reactive cells can reduce interferon-driven recruitment signals, while fibroblasts or myeloid cells can suppress the same signals. Ranking reflects the available case evidence and clinical relevance, not measured causality or a predicted drug response.
1 Poor immune recruitment and an immune-poor state
Low CXCR3 ligands across both research RNA samples and low BostonGene CXCL10; low CD3/NKG7 and non-inflamed portrait.
Chemokine shortage is a credible phenotype, but could reflect too few activated cells rather than an intrinsic recruitment defect.
Moderate archival support; current lesion and direction of causality unresolved.
Resection matrix RNA and selective B7 CAF proteins; CXCL12, THBS2 and ITGA5 leads.
Caris counterevidence, muscle/repair admixture and near-median CTHRC1/LRRC15 RNA weaken a uniform suppressive-CAF diagnosis.
Strong resection stromal phenotype; actual physical exclusion unmeasured.
CD39/CD73/ENPP1 detection, with downstream innate-signalling components.
No extracellular flux or current compartment measurements; CD39 can also mark useful T cells.
Coherent candidate, not demonstrated dependence or clinical eligibility biomarker.
Low resection antigen-display RNA, APC/PTEN changes and PTPN proteins.
Caris assay-matched results and retained bulk proteins oppose universal fixed loss.
A reversible or compositional explanation remains at least as plausible as an irreversible defect.
5 Myeloid suppression and clearance of dying cells
AXL/MERTK/GAS6/CSF1 and macrophage markers; SPP1 protein.
No proven SPP1-dominant suppressive niche; resident cells and cell mixture confound.
Plausible contributor, intertwined with recruitment/stroma rather than independent confirmation.
6 Insufficient priming or useful effector supply
Low TMB, blood lymphopenia and mixed T/NK/DC patterns; candidate design and intended innate adjuvant are documented.
No tumour-reactive clone or functional DC measurement. IL15 is high; CD1C/ITGAX and APC proteins argue against universal DC absence.
Priming quality, CD4 help, useful clonal breadth and expansion remain plausible gaps; none is a validated DC-drug selection marker. [VE1]
COX2/EP4 proteins unassigned; PGE2 unmeasured and CRC trials weak.
Secondary hypothesis with no predictive biomarker here.
Some endothelial/metabolic markers and historical liver CA9.
Caris VEGFA 6th and BostonGene 15th; no perfusion/oxygen data, rank-sensitive signatures.
A generic plausible mechanism, weakly selected by this case.
HLA-E and other checkpoint ligands; historical liver receptor RNA.
HLA-G protein assignment unconfirmed; receptor engagement and dominance unknown.
No evidence selects a particular alternative checkpoint as the main obstacle.

Missing function/localisation is an inference limit. No culture, organoid or tissue-slice programme is proposed; any further specimen testing depends on verified material and assay feasibility. [N2] [VE9]

PAGES.title: Specimens and the limits of current inference
blocks: This report integrates archival RNA/protein evidence, clinical sequencing, patient-level vactosertib trial analysis and vaccine-combination evidence. The focus is what available measurements and human studies justify now; additional tissue testing depends on verified material and assay feasibility. No organoid or culture programme is proposed. [N1] [N2] [VE1]
Clinical DNA/IHC, research RNA, and new assay-matched colorectal percentiles for five antigen-presentation genes.
Provider reports30% tumour and QC pass. New results describe this archival biopsy, not the recent node.
Targeted DNA panel and RNA; prior Salmon re-quantification retained.
30% tumour after microdissection per correspondence; not whole-exome coverage. No new broad clinical expression percentiles.
Bulk RNA with colorectal percentiles, genomic portrait and inferred microenvironment.
About15% tumour; treated specimen. Same surgical lesion as Tempus, not an independent metastasis.
Selected single-cell RNA summaries and CEA/other IHC.
Liver bulk sequencing failed QC. Selected summaries are not a full cell-by-gene matrix or spatial map.
Protein and precursor matrices; patient analytical run422; new immune-axis extraction.
B7 differs from B4; purity and precise section/aliquot chain unresolved. Run 423 and HPA control are not matched patient normals.
Histology confirms metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. Remaining material and suitability for additional assays require verification.
A1 extensive necrosis; A2 viable carcinoma reported, with very focal lymphoid tissue. No new node RNA/proteomic result located.
Caris Assure cell-free/buffy-coat RNA; ctDNA; vaccine candidates; TrufflePig analysis.
Blood RNA is not lesion RNA. TrufflePig/input provenance and selected merged-export columns do not create independent tumour evidence.
Collection date and assay/report date are distinct. BostonGene/Tempus tumour percentages must not be assigned to B7 or the node. Sources [C4] [C5] [C13] [C2] [C3] [C6] [C12] [C15] [P1] [C16].

The6November lymphocyte count was0.8x10^9/L and flagged low. This supports checking current lymphocyte subsets, collection yield and treatment timing; it does not diagnose absent tumour-specific T cells or justify a cytokine treatment by itself. RECIST nonmeasurability is no longer assumed: the user reports3November clinician advice that disease should be measurable, pending trial-site confirmation. [C17]

PAGES.title: Recruitment is one step in a linked immune process
blocks: What vaccines or N-803 might change
DCs take up and process vaccine antigen, receive activation/help signals, and prime useful CD4 and CD8 T cells.
MSS/low TMB permits neoantigens. Manufacture/predicted binding does not establish helper breadth, priming or natural tumour recognition.
Personalised vaccine with intended Hiltonol aims to generate antigen-specific responses. Delivery/activation must reach the relevant APCs; N-803 does not replace this step.
Useful T and NK cells expand and remain functional.
Recent peripheral lymphopenia and mixed effector RNA permit a shortage, but do not measure tumour-reactive cell number.
N-803 can expand/activate NK and CD8 cells through IL15 signalling. More circulating cells need not mean tumour control.
Chemokine gradients and vascular adhesion guide cells into the lesion.
CXCL9/10/11 are low in both research RNA samples; BostonGene CXCL10 is 3rd percentile. Vascular function is unmeasured.
Activated vaccine-specific cells or N-803-responsive cells could produce interferon-gamma and amplify chemokines. This is conditional and not demonstrated in this case.
Cells reach malignant epithelium rather than remain outside it.
Resection matrix and selective CAF proteins support stromal context; no spatial CD8 barrier is demonstrated.
Neither intervention directly removes collagen architecture or proves relief of TGF-beta/CXCL12 restraint.
Malignant cells naturally process retained targets and display peptide-HLA complexes recognised by effectors.
Resection low antigen-display RNA contrasts with near-median Caris results and retained bulk proteins. Fixed HLA/B2M loss is unproven.
Vaccine T cells still need their antigen-HLA target. N-803-enhanced NK cells may offer a partially HLA-independent route, but case-specific activity is unestablished.

This feedback loop matters: poor priming or expansion can produce little interferon-gamma, hence weak CXCL9/10 recruitment; poor recruitment can then prevent the local activation needed to sustain those chemokines. The current data cannot establish which direction started the problem. It is more accurate to describe an immune-poor recruitment state than a proven chemokine-pathway lesion. [N2]

The review framework is applied to this case as a hypothesis: it does not directly evaluate vactosertib or N-803. No human study establishes the complete regimen, its optimal timing or safety. [VE1] [VE9]

PAGES.title: Recruitment and effector evidence across the assays
blocks: NR means not reported/assigned, not biological absence. Research TPM, provider percentile and peptide count are different measurements. Low-abundance secreted proteins/rare immune cells are poorly excluded by bulk proteomic non-detection; PRF1 has only one source-labelled sequence. [N2]

The evidence is mixed: CD8A, KLRD1, GZMB and BATF3 are around the provider middle, while CD3D/E, CD8B and NKG7 are lower. BostonGene CD1C is 97th percentile and ITGAX 77th; B7 ITGAX has 15 source-labelled unique sequences. These oppose a blanket absence of antigen-presenting cells, without proving functional dendritic-cell priming. Rare-cell XCR1/CLEC9A RNA cannot yield a reliable cell count. The broad interferon-response set is method-sensitive; low chemokines do not establish global interferon-pathway failure.

PAGES.title: IL15 signalling and the case for Anktiva
blocks: BostonGene IL15 is at the 94th percentile, whereas IL15RA, IL2RB and IL2RG are at the 2nd, 10th and 6th. This does not establish an IL15 deficiency or an IL15-resistant tumour. Bulk receptor RNA may partly reflect the scarcity of relevant immune cells. It also cannot determine how responsive circulating or intratumoural NK/CD8 cells would be. [N2]

N-803 combines an IL15 agonist with an IL15-receptor-alpha/Fc complex, augmenting presentation and downstream stimulation of responsive immune cells. Low endogenous IL15RA RNA therefore does not exclude its action, but is not a validated biomarker selecting benefit. Conversely, high IL15 RNA does not prove the pathway is already maximally stimulated or that N-803 cannot add activity.

Historical liver single-cell data contained 2,231 CD8 and 1,732 NK cells; they are recovered cells, not unbiased tissue densities or tumour-reactivity measurements. Blood RNA is not current-lesion RNA. The 6 November lymphocyte count of 0.8 × 10^9/L supports a low circulating count, not a demonstrated shortage of antigen-specific clones. [C12] [C17] [N2]

PAGES.title: Personalised vaccines and immune priming
blocks: A personalised vaccine aims to create or broaden T cells that recognise selected tumour mutations. It has a direct role in priming, and human studies show that vaccine-induced cells can sometimes reach tumours. The evidence is stronger for generating immunity than for producing durable clinical benefit in MSS colorectal cancer, particularly after checkpoint therapy.
What this means for this case
Autogene cevumeran, personalised mRNA; phase I advanced cancers [NV1]

Immune responses in 10/11 evaluable MSS CRC patients. One patient with PD-L1-low MSS rectal cancer and small lung lesions had a complete response lasting 8.2 months on vaccine + atezolizumab. In a multicancer subset, vaccine-specific TCRs appeared in on-treatment tumour biopsies in 8/10 patients.

Positive evidence for priming and possible tumour homing. The 10/11 denominator describes immune responses, not tumour responses. The rectal responder’s prior-checkpoint status was not established. Detection in a biopsy does not prove contact with, or killing of, malignant cells.
NeoAg-VAX personalised peptides ± pembrolizumab; MSS mCRC pilot [NV2]

The abstract reports 2 partial responses among 28 treated (7.1%), median PFS 2.9 months, despite a median 5.9-fold increase in neoantigen-specific blood T-cell responses. Eight participants crossed from vaccine alone to combination treatment.

Directly relevant immunogenicity with modest clinical activity. The pooled response estimate cannot isolate the vaccine or pembrolizumab contribution. Prior-checkpoint composition was not stated in the retrieved abstract.
Four of six participants developed measurable neoantigen-specific immune responses; an illustrative patient had regressing liver lesions.
Supports feasibility. Six uncontrolled cases and responder-defined survival comparisons do not establish survival benefit.
GRANITE: randomised first-line MSS mCRC regimen [NV4]
Personalised viral/RNA vaccine plus checkpoint partners and standard care: PFS HR 0.73 (90% CI 0.44-1.21). Immune responses in 17/17 evaluable patients; short-term ctDNA response 39% versus 40%.
The confidence interval includes no benefit. A hypothesis-generating regimen-level signal in first-line care does not establish post-BOT/BAL benefit or a vaccine-specific effect.
Adjuvant mRNA monotherapy, ctDNA-positive resected CRC [NV5]
Randomised BNT122-01 was stopped in August 2026 after futility and a numerical overall-survival imbalance. The sponsor reported no new safety signal.
A substantial negative result. Different platform, earlier disease setting and no checkpoint partner prevent treating it as proof that every vaccine combination fails.

The peptide project has reported manufacture for 19 of 20 candidate targets and intended Hiltonol/poly-ICLC. Final released formulation, dosing and administration remain unconfirmed. Two explicit class-II annotations in the candidate list are a documentation limit, not proof that other peptides lack CD4 epitopes. Existing sequence evidence and the final design should be reconciled. [VE9]

PAGES.title: N803 immune expansion and the limits of clinical evidence
blocks: N-803 is an IL15 agonist complex that supports natural killer (NK) and CD8 T-cell activation, proliferation and survival. It can amplify available effectors, but does not supply tumour-antigen specificity. Human pharmacodynamic activity is clear; reliable clinical benefit in MSS CRC or after BOT/BAL has not been established.
QuEST1, mainly prostate cancer; separate MSS CRC subset [NV8]

Bintrafusp + N-803 produced one durable partial response among seven MSS/pMMR CRC patients. Prostate vaccine arms used shared brachyury antigen. Blood analyses showed NK/CD8 activation and expansion and stronger effector-to-suppressor ratios.

A rare CRC response supports investigation. Most outcomes and immune correlates are from prostate cancer; sequential nonrandomized arms do not isolate N-803 efficacy or establish restored CRC recruitment.
CV-301 shared CEA/MUC1 vaccine + N-803 + bintrafusp: 0/12 responses. Adding targeted IL12: 1/20; median PFS 1.8 months in both groups. The sole durable responder was checkpoint-naive.

Important negative CRC evidence for this multi-step combination concept. These were shared-antigen vaccines, not personalised neoantigens. The result does not prove vaccine antagonism or isolate any component.

Six partial responses among 21 treated; three among 11 previously progressing on PD1 blockade. Blood NK frequency more than doubled within seven days; CD8 proliferation and circulating interferon-gamma increased.
Evidence of biological activity and possible checkpoint resensitisation in another cancer. Exploratory, unconfirmed responses from an uncontrolled study are not an MSS CRC response estimate.
Randomised Lung-MAP S1800D, prior-checkpoint lung cancer [NV10]

Among 71 eligible acquired-resistance patients, N-803 + pembrolizumab did not significantly improve overall survival (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.40-1.36) or PFS (HR 1.29; 0.78-2.13) versus chemotherapy. Accrual closed at interim.
The stronger comparative evidence did not establish benefit. Numerical survival trends must not be presented as proven reversal of checkpoint resistance.
Twenty-four participants: NK-cell expansion and CD8 activation, but no complete or partial responses.
More or more-active immune cells in blood are insufficient by themselves; antigen recognition, access and local function still matter.

Systemic N-803 for CRC is investigational. The current licensed Anktiva product is for intravesical use with BCG; its label excludes subcutaneous, intravenous and intramuscular administration. The team must confirm the appropriate product/formulation, route and access arrangements. A commercial bladder vial is not established as a safe injectable product. [NV11]

QuICC’s abstract and Table 2 disagree about prior checkpoint exposure; no unreliable subgroup denominator is assigned. The sole durable responder was checkpoint-naive. The personalised vaccine/N-803/vactosertib/checkpoint proposal has no established efficacy or safety estimate. [NV9] [VE9]

PAGES.title: Where vaccines and N803 fit the case evidence
blocks: The available data suggest an immune-poor recruitment environment with residual immune machinery. They do not distinguish too few tumour-reactive clones from failed local recruitment, suppression after arrival, or incomplete tumour recognition. These are successive requirements, so improving one may leave another limiting step unchanged.

1 Priming
Generate the right antigen-specific T cells

Specialised dendritic-cell markers are mixed: BostonGene IRF8 5th percentile, but BATF3 55th, CD1C 97th and ITGAX 77th. B7 ITGAX/CD74/HLA-DRA proteins have 15/3/7 source-labelled unique peptides. These are not proof of functional cross-presentation or blanket dendritic-cell absence.

Vaccine with intended Hiltonol is the direct priming intervention. DC function, coordinated CD4/CD8 responses and natural cancer recognition remain unproved. FLT3L expansion and CD40 licensing are distinct research leads, not selected additions. [VE1]

2 Expansion and survival
Maintain useful T and NK cells

BostonGene IL15 itself is 94th percentile; IL15RA 2nd, IL2RB 10th and IL2RG 6th. Caris/Tempus IL15 research TPM is 6.55/6.45. CD4 and the leukocyte marker PTPRC proteins are present. Low receptor RNA may reflect cell mixture rather than defective signalling.

N-803 is a plausible expansion/activation adjunct. Neither low receptors nor recent lymphopenia is a validated predictor. Low endogenous IL15RA is not a requirement: N-803 already includes an IL15Ralpha component.

3 Recruitment
Attract effectors toward the lesion

Caris/Tempus CXCL9/10/11 TPM: 0.48/1.07/0 versus 1.81/1.68/0.91; all below the external-reference lower quartile. BostonGene CXCL10 3rd and CXCR3 4th percentiles. Low fragments and method-sensitive broad interferon signatures limit conclusions about pathway shutdown.

Vaccination or N-803 could indirectly stimulate an interferon-gamma-CXCL9/10/11 feedback loop, if useful cells can seed the lesion and local cells remain responsive. This is a conditional mechanism, not demonstrated repair of the chemokine gradient.

Resection CXCL12 is high (Tempus 96.5 TPM; BostonGene 99th percentile), with selective fibroblast/matrix proteins. Earlier Caris FN1 and VEGFA were 4th/6th percentiles; muscle and repair admixture remain alternatives to a physical barrier.

Neither vaccine nor N-803 directly removes matrix, normalises vessels or neutralises CXCL12. Biopsy detection of vaccine-specific clones in other patients shows entry can occur, not that it will occur here.

5 Recognition and killing
See and eliminate malignant cells

Low BostonGene antigen-display RNA contrasts with near-median Caris IRF1/TAP1/HLA-A/B and retained B7 HLA/B2M/TAP proteins. CD8A is 56th percentile in BostonGene; historical liver recovery included 2,231 CD8 T and 1,732 NK cells, without proof of tumour specificity.
Vaccine benefit requires retained targets and appropriate HLA display. N-803 may support CD8 and NK killing, but neither treatment guarantees recognition, contact, or resistance to local suppression.

The core proposal combines targeted priming, effector support, TGF-beta modulation and checkpoint blockade. Access discussions make it concrete, but each remaining bottleneck still needs interpretation. Prioritise final target/product reconciliation and a clinician-led sequence; no evidence supports indiscriminate extra-drug stacking. [VE9]

TPM values are independent research estimates, not vendor clinical TPM; the 18-sample public comparison is exploratory. Provider percentiles are assay-specific. B4 RNA and B7 protein are archival resection samples; liver counts are recovery-biased. Blood and unresolved Valius bulk data are retained in the source matrix but cannot establish tumour infiltration. [N2]

PAGES.title: Vaccine quality requires both priming and tumour recognition
blocks: A vaccine asks dendritic cells to teach the immune system a target; successful CD8 killing then asks malignant cells to display the same naturally processed target. These are separate checkpoints. CD4 help can operate through antigen-presenting cells without HLA class II on the cancer itself. The review does not make a platform or drug-count recommendation for this patient. [VE1]

Archival DNA/RNA support varies by candidate. Whole-gene TPM cannot show how much mutant transcript survives, particularly after a frameshift or premature stop. Current-node target retention/display is unknown.

Review exact mutant sequences, transcript support and sample timing; account for purity/copy number when interpreting clonality. Predicted binding or response to added peptide does not establish natural tumour recognition.

Long peptides can support both classes, but length/prediction does not establish actual helper/cytotoxic responses. Only two original entries explicitly annotate class-II restrictions; the others are not thereby proved to lack helper epitopes.
Audit the released sequences across HLA alleles and CD4/CD8 coverage. More candidates do not guarantee useful breadth; immunodominance can favour targets that do not mediate cancer killing.

Hiltonol/poly-ICLC is intended. Nineteen of twenty targets were reportedly manufactured; this is not a released-product or administration record. Final co-delivery/pooling details remain to be confirmed.
Reconcile the final design and delivery with the vaccine team. Antigen and activating signals must reach suitable APCs; an adjuvant’s presence alone does not show productive DC activation.
BostonGene IRF8 5th percentile contrasts with BATF3 55th, CD1C 97th and ITGAX 77th; B7 ITGAX/CD74/HLA-DRA have 15/3/7 source-labelled unique peptides.

A global DC absence diagnosis is unsupported. Lymph-node vaccine priming and intratumour DC recruitment/restimulation are different compartments; FLT3L or CD40 sensitivity cannot be inferred from bulk markers.

Low resection IRF1/TAP/HLA RNA contrasts with Caris assay-matched results and retained bulk proteins. Beta-2-microglobulin supports stable HLA-I; the old B2M cysteine-to-arginine change at position 100 is an unvalidated research call.
Broader targets/HLA alleles may limit single-target escape, but cannot bypass complete HLA-I pathway loss. Complete loss is not established here, so uncertainty is not proof of vaccine futility.

Immediate priorities are documentary and available-data reconciliation; no culture or organoid programme is proposed. Future clinically obtained immune results should distinguish specificity, CD4/CD8 balance, clonal breadth and persistence from simple lymphocyte expansion. [VE1] [VE9] [N2]

PAGES.title: The proposed combination and access through Asthra
blocks: I am planning a four-component strategy with Dr Santosh Kesari at Asthra Health. This is a concrete proposal with access discussions underway, not an administered regimen or a demonstrated way to overcome resistance. Doses and timing must be determined by the treating team; no safe or optimal full-combination schedule has been established. [VE9] [VE16]
Personalised JLF peptide vaccine with intended Hiltonol
Prime and broaden tumour-specific T cells through antigen-presenting cells.
Asthra vaccine delivery has been discussed; manufacture of 19/20 targets reported. Final release, actual vial contents and administration unconfirmed.
Manufacture/prediction does not prove CD4/CD8 breadth, natural target display or tumour control.
Investigate TGF-beta-associated stromal and immune restraint.
On 6 November Dr Kesari said his team would add me to its single-patient IND access list. Sponsor agreement, approvals and supply remain unconfirmed.
13/103 evaluable CRC responses was an overall CRC denominator, not exclusively confirmed MSS. Prior checkpoint therapy was excluded; trial RNA supplied no positive selector (all q=.521).
Support responsive NK/CD8 activation, proliferation and survival.
Access through Asthra has been discussed. Systemic CRC use is investigational; formulation, route and access arrangements need confirmation.
Commercial intravesical Anktiva is not established as a safe injectable product. Expansion supplies neither tumour specificity nor reliable recruitment or recognition.
Sustain activity of responsive tumour-reactive T cells.
Pembrolizumab was discussed. BOT/BAL is an alternative checkpoint component requiring new clinical justification and renewed sponsor approval.
Balstilimab already blocks PD-1; BOT/BAL is not an automatic extra PD-1 drug. Previous progression limits rechallenge inference; CTLA-4 adds immune toxicity.

The aim is complementary biology, not maximal simultaneous treatment. Interactions and overlapping inflammatory or gastrointestinal toxicity can offset benefit. Updated disease assessment and continued control with clinician-directed systemic care matter; the proposal does not establish failure of irinotecan/panitumumab.

Status reviewed 18 November 2026. The patient is aiming for vaccine treatment in early 2027; no complete-regimen start, final access approval or administration is confirmed. The low-response QuICC results and negative comparative N-803 evidence remain important counterweights. [VE9] [NV9] [NV10] [NV11] [VR1]

PAGES.title: Research priorities for dendritic cells and vaccine delivery
blocks: These are additional research leads within axis 6 (priming and useful effectors). Existing order remains tumour-reactive TCR therapy, personalised vaccination with an immune partner, then an N-803-supported vaccine/checkpoint strategy. The next three leads address different priming steps. Their order is a discussion priority, not a comparative response prediction; all remain tier 5 in the overall therapeutic shortlist. [VE9]
Expand antigen-presenting dendritic cells, complementing N-803’s main NK/CD8 effects. Expanded cells still need activation.

Randomised resected-melanoma vaccine study (n=60) improved DC abundance and antigen-specific immunity. It did not establish clinical-benefit superiority or CRC efficacy. Bulk case markers do not diagnose a responsive DC shortage. [VE3]

NeoVax/CDX-301 melanoma study is active, not recruiting; no open CRC route verified. Celldex physician enquiry is possible, but its linked older policy says products are unavailable for compassionate use. Supply remains unconfirmed. [VE10] [VE13]
Provide DC licensing/co-stimulation involved in helper-T-cell support. It does not replace all CD4 functions.

Local melanoma vaccine study: 22 treated, ex-vivo helper-peptide responses in 6/22, persistent in only 1/22; no dose-limiting or grade 3+ treatment-related toxicity. Immunogenicity was modest; comparisons with earlier adjuvants were not randomised. No CRC efficacy. [VE4]

Broad CRC-eligible phase I completed. Other studies are closed or cancer-specific; no accepting CRC route or individual supply confirmed. Local-study tolerability does not establish systemic CD40 safety with this combination. [VE11] [VE13]
6 Multi-adjuvant delivery with local CTLA-4 blockade
Review antigen/adjuvant co-delivery and local priming. NeoVaxMI used peptides, poly-ICLC, Montanide, local ipilimumab and systemic nivolumab.

Eleven enrolled, ten vaccinated, nine completed; CD8 responses in 6/9 fully vaccinated. Mostly resected melanoma, uncontrolled: individual contributions and CRC efficacy cannot be isolated. Hiltonol is already intended here. [VE2]

Published trial is melanoma-specific and closed to recruitment. Any adaptation requires the vaccine team’s formulation/delivery review. Local ipilimumab evidence does not validate repeating systemic BOT/BAL. [VE12]

Direct CD8 killing still requires natural cancer-cell peptide-HLA display. No demonstrated benefit justifies adding any of these as an empirical fifth drug. Readiness of the existing vaccine and access discussions should not be mistaken for confirmation of these additional interventions.

PAGES.title: Metabolic leads and limits imposed by the disease setting
blocks: BAY-8002 rescued glycan-conditioned healthy-donor DC functions in laboratory experiments. Separate AZD3965 phase I experience included 20 enrolled CRC patients but no objective solid-tumour responses. These different compounds/models do not establish tumour-specific vaccine benefit or a case DC lactate-flux defect. [VE5] [VE6]
AZD3965 trial completed; no active matched route identified. Retinal, cardiac-troponin and acidosis toxicities limited dose. Laboratory BAY-8002 availability is not clinical supply. [VE14]

Glutamate-cysteine ligase catalyses the first, rate-limiting step in glutathione synthesis. A melanoma mouse study combined BSO depletion with Flt3L and intratumoral poly(I:C)/anti-CD40, not a loaded DC vaccine. Tumour ferroptosis may also contribute. Historical BSO/melphalan human studies establish exposure, not CRC vaccine benefit or selective DC restoration. [VE7] [VE8]

No active matched trial or established supply identified; historical studies completed/withdrawn. Normal cells also require glutathione. Chemotherapy-combination toxicity and stem-cell-supported experience cannot establish safety for this immune strategy. [VE15]
Disease setting and sequencing affect what can be inferred

Evidence after complete resection cannot be transferred directly to active metastatic CRC, even when tumour volume is small. The review discusses de-novo priming, pre-existing clones and checkpoint timing as context-dependent possibilities. Preclinical sequence effects do not define a universal clinical schedule. No dosing or timing prescription follows for vactosertib, N-803, vaccine and PD-1 blockade. [VE1]

Randomised trials illustrate the setting distinction. After complete melanoma resection, INTerpath001 (1,137 participants) improved 24-month recurrence-free survival with intismeran/pembrolizumab: 82.2% versus 70.0% with placebo/pembrolizumab (P<.001). In advanced melanoma, IMcode001 (125 participants) found no significant PFS improvement with autogene cevumeran/pembrolizumab: 8.3 versus 7.9 months (P=.3061), with response rates 41.7% versus 48.8%, despite vaccine immune responses in 47/56 assessed. These are different products and populations, not a direct setting or platform comparison. They show why blood immunogenicity cannot establish benefit in this active CRC proposal. [VE17] [VE18]

The CRC counterevidence remains substantial: QuICC had 0/12 responses without targeted IL12 and 1/20 with it; the sole durable responder was checkpoint-naive. The trial used a shared-antigen vaccine and bintrafusp, so it neither tests this exact personalised regimen nor isolates any component. A personalised-peptide pilot produced increased blood responses but only 2/28 tumour responses. The resected-CRC BNT122-01 programme stopped for futility; earlier-stage treatment is not a guarantee. [NV9] [NV2] [NV5]

Repeat BOT/BAL alone remains last within axis 6 (rank 9): no new overcoming mechanism has been demonstrated. Blood immunogenicity, cytokine activation, target expression and access are not validated surrogates for tumour control. The five research leads do not change the vactosertib result: four primary tests, all q=.521, with small-sample/archival limits. [VR1]

PAGES.title: What the vactosertib clinical trial establishes
blocks: Vactosertib inhibits signalling through TGF-beta-related receptor kinases; pembrolizumab blocks PD-1. Their combination produced occasional durable responses in non-MSI-high colorectal cancer, but most participants did not respond. This uncontrolled trial does not establish how much benefit vactosertib adds to pembrolizumab or identify a validated molecular responder profile. [VT1] [VT2]

Open-label phase Ib/IIa at five Korean centres: 120 treated, including 108 CRC and 12 gastric cancer. Prior checkpoint therapy was prohibited; measurable disease and ECOG performance status 0-1 were required. [VT2]
This does not test rescue after botensilimab/balstilimab (BOT/BAL).
13/103 evaluable CRC patients had a partial response (12.6%); disease control was 28.2%. Five treated CRC patients lacked a follow-up scan: four deteriorated rapidly and one died early. [VT1] [VT3]
The all-treated response fraction is 13/108 (12.0%), a descriptive sensitivity calculation, not the published primary estimate. [VT6]
Median progression-free survival was 1.2 months; median response duration was 12.5 months among responders. Median overall survival was 13.2 months. [VT1]
Durable benefit in a minority coexisted with early progression in many. Uncontrolled survival cannot isolate the treatment effect.
Unplanned subgroup: 9/40 responses without active liver metastases (22.5%) versus 4/63 with liver metastases (6.3%); median progression-free survival approximately 1.4 versus 1.2 months. [VT1] [VT5]
A clinically relevant association, not a validated treatment-selection rule. Historical resected liver disease is not the same as active liver disease at entry.
Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22/120 (18.3%, CRC and gastric cohorts combined); one sudden death was considered possibly treatment-related. [VT1]
These results do not establish the safety of adding a vaccine, N-803 or another immunotherapy.
Clinical and blood biomarkers did not provide a reliable responder test

Exploratory baseline comparisons included 13 responders versus 90 nonresponders. Tumour mutation burden was similar (median 6.6 versus 6.2 mutations/Mb; P = .609; available in 12 and 86 patients), as was the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (3.3 versus 3.1; P = .933). Mutation and prior-treatment comparisons were limited by missingness and small groups. [VT5]

In 75 patients, early blood changes in TGF-beta1, PAI-1, CTGF and PDGF were examined. PAI-1 fell more at higher doses, but changes did not significantly distinguish the 10 partial responders from 65 nonresponders. A blood change after dosing is evidence of drug effect, not a baseline response predictor; tissue SERPINE1 expression cannot substitute for that PAI-1 measurement. [VT2] [VT3]

PAGES.title: Vactosertib biomarker changes and tumour response
blocks: We linked the deposited subject-level clinical records to the paired tissue measurements and examined the RNA worksheets and transparent peer-review file. This secondary audit resolves a critical ambiguity: the reported favourable immune-cell changes were measured in a subset with no confirmed objective responders. [VT3] [VT4] [VT6]

Tumour-nest analysis: 19 patients. Stromal analysis: 22 for total CD8/Treg and 20 for granzyme-B-positive CD8/Treg. All subsets contained zero objective responders and only two durable-stable-disease cases meeting clinical benefit.
These samples cannot reveal pretreatment features of patients whose tumours shrank. The authors explain that post-treatment tissue from confirmed partial responders was unavailable. [VT3] [VT4]

Among patients without clinical benefit, the granzyme-B-positive CD8/Treg ratio increased in 15/17 tumour-nest pairs and 17/18 stromal pairs. Clinical benefit means response or stable disease lasting at least six months.

A shift toward cytotoxic-cell markers can occur without durable disease control. A ratio can change through either its numerator or denominator; it is not a direct measure of tumour-cell killing. [VT6]

For the two benefit cases versus nonbenefit cases, median baseline granzyme-B-positive CD8/Treg was 0.105 versus 0.129 in tumour nests (n = 2/17), and 0.226 versus 0.195 in stroma (n = 2/18). All baseline ratios are retained in the audit.
Two durable stable-disease cases and zero objective responders cannot define a useful cutoff. Bulk case RNA/protein cannot be substituted for these compartment-specific cell ratios. [VT6]

12 at 200 mg twice daily and 16 at 300 mg twice daily. SMAD2 decreased at the higher dose (adjusted P = .0057); SMAD6 increase was not significant. The 21-gene figure selects differences between dose-group fold changes.
This is an on-treatment pathway analysis, not a baseline responder classifier. The 21 genes are not necessarily 21 statistically significant treatment changes. [VT2] [VT3]

An exploratory analysis used five benefit cases versus 29 nonbenefit cases. Benefit included partial response or durable stable disease. Immune/interferon programmes rose in the benefit group; the authors excluded this imbalanced analysis from the final results.
Do not merge this 34-patient population with the published 28: their mapping is not supplied. Response-associated change after treatment does not predict response from baseline RNA. [VT4]

CD8 marks a T-cell population; granzyme B is a cytotoxic-effector marker; FOXP3-positive regulatory T cells are the denominator labelled Treg. The public RNA workbook contains 34,769 gene-level dose-contrast summaries, not individual baseline expression linked to response. Its DESeq2 baseMean is an average normalized count, not baseline TPM. That table alone cannot support a valid case-versus-responder expression score. [VT3] [VT6]

The complete raw-read baseline analysis now includes all 28 screening-labelled samples, with clinical benefit (5 versus 23) primary and objective response (2 versus 26) secondary. None of the four fixed TGF-beta/fibroblast/matrix programs showed a significant association. The following pages distinguish these baseline results from the published on-treatment RNA changes. [VR1] [VR2]

PAGES.title: Baseline trial RNA does not establish a responder selection rule
blocks: We reprocessed all 28 available screening-labelled RNA samples from the vactosertib plus pembrolizumab trial and tested four published gene programs selected before inspecting pathway scores. None was significantly associated with study-defined clinical benefit after correcting for the four primary tests. The data do not validate high TGF-beta, fibroblast or matrix expression as a positive selection marker for this treatment. They also do not establish absence of benefit. [VR1] [VR2]

Clinical benefit is confirmed response OR stable disease maintained for at least six months: 5 patients met this definition and 23 did not. The six-month criterion applies to stable disease, not necessarily to each response. Scores average the within-sample expression ranks of member genes among 19,557 coding genes, on a 0-100 scale. They are not colorectal-population percentiles or response probabilities.

Fibroblast TGF-beta response
Pan-fibroblast signature, 19 genes

LRRC15-associated fibroblast state
Cancer-associated fibroblasts, 11 genes

Cancer-associated extracellular matrix
Matrix-up program, 30 genes

Estimated shift is the Hodges-Lehmann median of every benefit-minus-nonbenefit pairwise difference; it is not subtraction of the two group medians. P values use exact two-sided rank-sum label permutations; q values use Benjamini-Hochberg correction within the four primary tests. No effect confidence intervals were implemented in the frozen analysis. All primary medians are lower in the benefit group, but these uncertain differences do not justify either a high- or low-expression selection rule.

Hallmark is a broad curated TGF-beta response program. The pan-fibroblast set includes contractile genes and can reflect smooth-muscle admixture. The LRRC15-associated set includes CTHRC1 and other fibroblast-state genes. The extracellular-matrix set captures a cancer-associated matrix program. Bulk scores combine cell abundance and cell state; none directly measures receptor activation or spatial exclusion. Exact memberships are supplied, with no outcome-driven selection. [VR3] [VR4] [VR5] [VR6]

PAGES.title: Pathway scores overlap across the clinical benefit groups
blocks: Each point is one of the 28 baseline trial samples. Horizontal lines show group medians. The primary comparisons use all 5 benefit and all 23 nonbenefit samples; no subject was excluded on the basis of outcome or pathway score. [VR1]

Unlabelled individual observations show the distribution and overlap rather than a proposed cutoff. Scores use the same within-sample coding-gene rank scale in each panel. Clinical benefit means confirmed response or stable disease maintained at least six months. No panel supplies a validated treatment-selection threshold.

The programs are biologically related, but their exact memberships are not identical: the 54-gene Hallmark set shares no genes with the other three frozen sets; the pan-fibroblast and LRRC15-associated sets share two and four genes, respectively, with the matrix set. Association is not causation or treatment-specific prediction.

PAGES.title: Secondary and sensitivity analyses support the same limited conclusion
blocks: Objective tumour response was an explicitly secondary endpoint: 2 responders versus 26 nonresponders in this RNA subset. Its response fraction is not a replacement for the full trial response rate. Lower fibroblast and matrix point estimates in the two responders are descriptive; the secondary four-test correction does not establish a response biomarker. [VR1]

Fibroblast TGF-beta response
Pan-fibroblast signature, 19 genes

LRRC15-associated fibroblast state
Cancer-associated fibroblasts, 11 genes

Cancer-associated extracellular matrix
Matrix-up program, 30 genes

Mean log2(TPM + 1), a stricter expressed-gene universe, permutations within dose groups, and permutations jointly within dose and liver-status groups produced no nominal P below .05 for any program or endpoint. Hallmark and matrix clinical-benefit median directions change under log scoring, illustrating dependence on the expression metric. These checks did not change eligibility, endpoints or gene memberships after seeing outcomes.

Both objective responders received 200 mg twice daily and had no liver involvement in the supplied baseline site lists. Stratification reduces these specific imbalances but cannot remove unmeasured confounding. The joint dose/liver response test has only 21 admissible label allocations, so its resolution is intrinsically coarse. A sensitivity test with very few possible allocations cannot establish equivalence.

The primary unstratified tests enumerate all 98,280 allocations; secondary tests enumerate 378. Dose-stratified and joint dose/liver counts are 26,400 and 2,100 for clinical benefit, and 66 and 21 for response. All 24 scoring/endpoint rows, 72 exact tests and effect calculations were independently reproduced. [VR1]

PAGES.title: Trial RNA quality and clinical limits constrain interpretation
blocks: 23/28 pre/post collection intervals exceed 90 days; median interval 834 days. Biopsy organ is unknown in the available mapping.
This is the interval between specimens, not directly tissue age at first dose. Archival biology, tissue composition and selection into the paired-RNA subset can confound outcomes.
Median transcript mapping 30.28% of retained pairs; range 4.70-39.23%. Eleven samples are below 20%. Estimated coding fragments range 1.35-13.11 million.
Total-RNA libraries contain non-exonic and ribosomal reads excluded by the transcript reference. Low mapping is a documented limitation; it did not become an outcome-based exclusion.
Median coding fragments 2.86 million with clinical benefit versus 6.88 million without.
Broad gene detection does not eliminate technical confounding. No post-hoc depth filter or outcome-driven correction was introduced.
24 libraries detected as expected reverse-stranded; four had weak directionality and were accepted as unstranded after independent, outcome-blind review.
Automatic library detection remained enabled uniformly. Unstranded compatibility of 100% is expected from acceptance of both orientations, not evidence of superior quality.
All 28 outputs have the same 233,652 transcript IDs. All 54/19/11/30 pathway members are represented in the primary universe.
Missing rows were not converted into zero. The stricter universe excludes measured low-expression LEFTY2 and NOG from Hallmark; all four sets remain eligible.
Only 5 benefit cases and 2 responders; dose, liver status, mutation burden, tissue purity and sample availability vary.
A single-arm association cannot distinguish prognosis from treatment-specific prediction or isolate vactosertib from pembrolizumab. Prior checkpoint-treated patients were excluded from the trial.

The same GENCODE 37 transcript reference and Salmon 2.8 point-estimation approach used for the case RNA were applied to all 28 trial samples. Kit-aware Cutadapt preprocessing removed adapters and the first three read-2 bases; raw downloads were checksum-verified. Gene TPM includes all transcript contributions to coding genes. Fixed memberships, analysis code, aggregate QC and results, reference hashes and independent checks accompany the report. Full upstream reproduction requires the external public raw reads and published clinical source data. [VR1] [VR2]

The initial technical pilot and subsequent preprocessing/runtime/library amendments are preserved in the provenance. Endpoints, four programs and tests remained fixed before pathway scoring. This analysis supplies no current-case calibration, SMAD4-specific efficacy test, paired-treatment response model or independently validated classifier.

PAGES.title: Assessing the case for vactosertib benefit
blocks: The present evidence supports a plausible investigational option, but does not support describing this tumour as likely to respond. The strongest case-specific signals establish possible stromal and recruitment mechanisms; the trial did not validate those signals as predictors of benefit. No defensible individual response probability follows from the available data.
Stromal RNA and selective fibroblast proteins

Treated-resection matrix RNA and B7 proteins support stromal biology. In our complete 28-sample trial analysis, none of four baseline TGF-beta/fibroblast/matrix programs was associated significantly with clinical benefit (all q = .521). Muscle/repair admixture remains important.
Biological rationale persists, but no positive high-stroma responder marker is established. This small analysis does not exclude benefit. [VR1] [VT1-VT6]

Low IFNG/CXCL9/10/11 expression is compatible with poor recruitment, priming or local activation. It does not clearly match the more inflamed baseline phenotype associated with favourable INCA33890 outcomes.
Reason for caution, not proof of resistance. A weak baseline signal does not prove that treatment cannot induce it; INCA33890 is also a different drug. [VT7]

CD274 (PD-L1) is at the 48th/71st Caris/BostonGene percentiles; PDCD1 (PD-1) is at the 60th/84th. They are not uniformly low. These bulk RNA ranks do not measure PD-L1-positive tissue area or receptor coexpression on the same cells.
Cannot apply INCA33890 protein-staining cutoffs to the case RNA percentiles. [VT7] [VT8]
Caris/Tempus values around 5/4.2 mutations/Mb are compatible with the low-mutation-burden vactosertib population. Its baseline mutation burden did not distinguish responders.
Neither a strong positive selector nor proof response is impossible. Tissue mutation burden is not interchangeable with INCA33890 blood mutation burden. [VT5] [VT7]
The vactosertib trial excluded previous immune-checkpoint therapy. It did not establish restored sensitivity after botensilimab/balstilimab.
Major limit on applying its response rate to this case. A proposed combination is not evidence of post-BOT/BAL efficacy. [VT2]

If contemporary assessment confirms no active liver metastases, the more favourable trial subgroup is closer clinically. Archival biopsy, treated-resection blocks and selected liver data do not establish the molecular state of current nodal disease.
Conditional favourable context, not a validated predictor. Historical liver resection and current liver involvement must be distinguished. [VT1]

Among stromal immunotherapy approaches, vactosertib plus pembrolizumab merits discussion because it has direct human CRC activity and occasional durable responses. It should remain an investigational candidate rather than a biomarker-selected likely success. Expression alone does not justify moving it ahead of treatments with stronger applicable clinical efficacy evidence, or assuming that adding further immune agents will overcome the remaining barriers.

A treatment-associated biomarker can be prognostic (related to outcome generally) or reflect drug effect. A predictive marker should identify differential benefit from the treatment; the uncontrolled studies here do not validate that distinction. The case comparison uses existing data and does not depend on additional tissue consumption.

PAGES.title: SMAD4 G359E functional evidence and clinical uncertainty
blocks: SMAD4 helps transmit TGF-beta signals to gene regulation. G359E replaces glycine with glutamate at position 359. Monash investigators report strongly impaired signalling in their screen. Caris’s machine-readable variant file annotates this allele CI=VUS, but G359E is not listed in the printed clinical variant tables. The Monash investigators also retain an overall variant-of-uncertain-significance (VUS) assessment. The direct assay strengthens functional evidence; it does not itself settle clinical pathogenicity. [SM1] [SM12] [SM14]
Monash investigators place G359E in their strong damaging assay category and consider the result to support PS3 functional evidence (personal communication, 17 November 2026). [SM14]

The public methods describe restoration of a GFP TGF-beta reporter in SMAD4-inactivated HT29 colorectal cells. Supports a defect in this response; raw score, replication, error-bar definition and calibration were not independently reviewed. [SM12]
Caris: 477/1,752 DNA reads (27.2%), with support on both strands. Research reanalysis: 424/1,578 tumour versus 0/233 matched-normal allele-supporting basecalls. [SM1]
Strong evidence that the mutation is real and tumour acquired. These analyses use the same primary sequencing; they do not demonstrate persistence in metastases or functional damage.
Retained primary-biopsy RNA audit: 251/550 eligible fragments carry G359E (45.6%). [SM1]
Supports mutant RNA expression. It does not establish mutant-protein abundance, loss of function or antigen presentation.
AlphaMissense 0.933, REVEL 0.908 and CADD 31 favour damage; EVE 0.302 is labelled benign. [SM8]
These correlated predictions are less direct than the new assay for the functional question. The benign EVE label does not negate the measured defect; none of these scores is a clinical probability.
BoostDM COADREAD labels G359E Driver, score 0.61; its pan-cancer score is 0.25. Conservation supports the colorectal prediction; its 3D-clustering feature is zero. [SM9]
Supports a colorectal driver hypothesis, with model-dependent uncertainty. A model label is not a clinical oncogenicity classification or evidence of drug sensitivity.
Our audit finds glycine-favoured backbone geometry in several wild-type structures. Replacing it with bulkier, acidic glutamate could disturb local structure. [SM10]

Mechanistic inference only. Gly359 does not make the direct interchain contacts seen for nearby R361. No G359E mutant structure was modelled; the new functional result does not identify the molecular cause of impairment.
One exact somatic G359E occurs in a public primary rectal-adenocarcinoma record. The gnomAD query returned no variant; site coverage was not verified. [SM11]
Disease-relevant corroboration, not a statistical hotspot. Rarity is not proof of harm. A published residue-359 frameshift is a different alteration. [SM13]

Conclusion: G359E has experimentally supported impairment in the tested TGF-beta response. This does not establish complete loss of every SMAD4 function, a dominant-negative effect, loss of both functional copies or persistence in the current lesion. No G359E-specific vactosertib sensitivity was supplied. [SM14]

PAGES.title: SMAD4 and TGF beta signalling in tumour and stromal cells
blocks: The exact-variant functional result makes impaired canonical SMAD4 signalling more credible in cells expressing G359E. It does not automatically disable TGF-beta responses in surrounding fibroblasts or immune cells. Tumour-cell impairment can therefore coexist with a stromal rationale for TGF-beta inhibition, without making G359E a treatment-selection biomarker. [SM5-SM7] [SM14]
Is this alteration present throughout the current cancer?

Primary-biopsy DNA and RNA support it; resection RNA shows 0/58 eligible mutant fragments. Caris’s printed appendix lists SMAD4 and SMAD2 copy number as indeterminate (PDF page 20). Resection tumour-DNA confirmation and current-node/liver allele evidence were not established. [SM1] [C4]

The RNA result does not prove loss of the DNA clone: expression, cell mixture and sampling differ. Indeterminate copy number establishes neither loss nor retention of the other allele. Do not assume all lesions carry G359E.
Does high SMAD4 expression mean normal function?

BostonGene RNA ranks at the CRC 100th percentile; B7 protein is detected with four source-labelled unique peptide sequences. Other SMAD4 mutants can remain abundant despite impaired signalling. [SM1] [SM5]
Bulk RNA/protein cannot distinguish functional wild-type protein, stable mutant protein and surrounding normal cells. High abundance neither proves nor excludes impaired tumour-cell signalling.
What changes if tumour-cell SMAD4 is impaired?

Canonical signalling through SMAD2/3-SMAD4 may weaken, including growth-restraint signals; some other receptor-dependent signals can remain. Nearby R361 mutants also have distinct Wnt effects, which cannot be assigned to G359E. [SM5] [SM6]
Low epithelial pathway output need not mean low TGF-beta exposure. A high fibroblast signature can coexist with impaired canonical signalling in cancer cells.

A CRC mouse study included both epithelial Tgfbr2 loss and a separate CRISPR Smad4-knockout model. Galunisertib suppressed metastatic capacity in the Smad4-knockout arm. Neither model tested G359E or vactosertib. [SM7]
Supports compatibility of the two mechanisms, not a personal efficacy estimate. Bulk fibroblast abundance and pathway activity still require separate interpretation.
The protocol cites a rationale involving SMAD4-deficient models and another inhibitor, LY2109761. The published clinical package reports no SMAD4-genotype response analysis. [SM2] [SM3] [SM4] [SM6]

The new functional evidence strengthens one biological premise, but does not justify raising the treatment rank or estimated response probability. Neither this assay nor the protocol demonstrates genotype-specific clinical benefit. [SM14]
Functional evidence and clinical classification answer different questions

PS3 is a functional-evidence criterion in the ACMG/AMP germline framework, not a final pathogenic classification. The investigator assigns this evidence while retaining VUS overall; this report has not independently calibrated its strength. Absent family observations do not themselves make an acquired tumour variant benign or prevent classification. Somatic oncogenicity and treatment sensitivity require separate assessment. [SM14] [SM15] [SM16]

Useful existing-data follow-up is the exact score, confidence/error definition, independent replication, controls and threshold calibration, alongside existing tumour copy-number and later-lesion allele records if available. These are evidence-review questions, not proposals for new patient-derived culture experiments.

PAGES.title: Evidence for SMAD4 independent signalling across the case
blocks: TGF-beta can signal through ERK and other routes without the usual SMAD4-containing transcriptional complex. The case data show that relevant components are present and that the treated resection has a strong early-response gene programme. They do not establish that TGF-beta drives ERK in the malignant cells, or that this route explains treatment resistance. [NC2] [NC3] [NC4] [NC5] [NC9]
The published ten-gene MAPK-response set is measurable. Clinical CCND1 expression is 90th percentile. EGFR, MET and FGFR3 are 94th, 82nd and 96th percentiles.

The ten-gene rank summary exceeds only 10/18 external CRC references. Only CCND1 and EPHA2 have supplied Caris percentiles within this set; EPHA2 is 52nd. Other growth-factor receptors offer alternative inputs.
A separate 20-gene immediate-early panel exceeds 17/18 references using total transcripts and 18/18 using coding transcripts. It includes FOS, EGR and DUSP response genes.

The published ten-gene MAPK set exceeds 6/18 references by total-transcript rank and only 1/18 with coding transcripts. Stress, treatment, repair and tissue composition can produce early-response signals.
TGFBR1/2 are both 99th percentile; TGFB2/3 both 98th. Early-response examples include EGR1 96th, DUSP5 99th, FOSB 97th and FOSL2 100th.

The ten MAPK-member percentiles have a descriptive median of 35; four are below 25. DUSP4/6 are 40th/33rd, SPRY2/4 7th/19th and ETV4/EPHA2 both 1st. This is another assay of the same specimen, not another lesion.

B7 resection proteome
Same operation, different block
ERK2 and ERK1 are confidently detected: 11 and 13 gene-specific peptide sequences remain after checking sequence ambiguity. TGF-beta1 and FOS are also detected.
Total ERK abundance is broadly reference-like. No phosphorylation measurement was supplied. Mixed bowel-wall, stromal and malignant tissue prevents assigning the signal to a particular cell type.

Valius liver
Selected RNA and IHC
EPHA2 RNA is reported in 70.73% of tumour cells; EGFR, FGFR2/3 and MET are also detected. MET staining has an H-score of 160.

Only EPHA2 of the ten MAPK genes is in the selected 101-gene RNA export. No full liver expression matrix, global proteome or phospho-ERK result was available. Receptor presence is not receptor activation.

Valius bulk column
Specimen linkage unresolved
All ten MAPK genes have reported expression values.
Its specimen/pipeline assignment remains unresolved. It cannot be treated as independent liver or current-node confirmation; secondary explorer views are not new assays.
Blood cell-free RNA and buffy-coat-associated RNA
Both tables contain all ten MAPK genes; their values remain in the source table.
These are separate blood-associated measurements, not extra tumour biopsies. Their mixture cannot establish tumour-cell pathway activity.
No corresponding RNA, global protein or phospho-ERK result was located.
The current lesion cannot be assigned the pathway state of the archival 2024 tissues.

The external comparison uses 18 primary CRC samples from GSE50760 processed with the same quantifier and reference. Counts such as 10/18 are research ordering counts, not clinical percentiles. Caris’s November supplement supplies five other genes and adds no MAPK-signature percentiles. [NC1]

PAGES.title: ERK evidence depends on the measurement
blocks: The published MAPK Pathway Activity Score (MPAS) uses these ten genes: PHLDA1, SPRY2, SPRY4, DUSP4, DUSP6, CCND1, EPHA2, EPHA4, ETV4 and ETV5. All are available in the research Caris and Tempus matrices. We reused this membership with transparent exploratory scoring; we did not apply a validated clinical MPAS cutoff. [NC1] [NC9]
Ranks are calculated within each sample across the same 19,619 coding-gene universe, then averaged across the ten genes. Neither sample is consistently near the top of the reference distribution.
The original whole-transcriptome denominator is retained. Caris remains near the middle; the resection falls toward the low end.
This alternative normalization looks substantially higher. It uses gene-level log2(TPM+1) z-scores from the 18 reference samples, summed and divided by sqrt(10).
Reference log-z summary, coding transcripts only
The apparent elevation weakens or reverses. For example, CCND1 is 3,538.46 total versus 61.61 coding TPM in Caris, and 251.57 versus 1.93 in Tempus. Transcript allocation matters.

“Above x/18” means x reference samples had a lower score; it is not a response probability or clinical percentile. The original MPAS formula is assay-relative. Our log transformation and external reference differ from its original implementation. Library preparation, treatment, purity and site remain confounders despite consistent computational quantification. [NC1]
Against 27 Astral CRC references, ERK2/MAPK1 and ERK1/MAPK3 rank shifts are −1.79 and +3.44 points. Upstream MEK/adaptor proteins are mixed.
Normal total abundance does not exclude an activated kinase. Conversely, confidently detecting ERK does not demonstrate its activation.
TGF-beta1 has four source-labelled unique sequences; its Astral rank shift is +28.83 points. FOS has two independently gene-specific sequences and a +19.86-point shift.
These are total-protein observations, not active ligand, receptor dependence or a complete ERK-response programme. MPAS protein coverage is insufficient for a score.
The delivered output contains no phosphorylation annotations among 75,443 positive patient precursor rows; no phosphosite quantification or phospho-ERK stain was located.
This was not a negative phospho-ERK test. Activation is unmeasured, not shown to be absent. No phospho-AKT result is established either.

PAGES.title: What the findings mean for SMAD4 and treatment hypotheses
blocks: G359E now has variant-specific evidence of impaired SMAD4-dependent transcription in an experimental model. Three further questions remain unresolved: its effect in the current tumour, whether a noncanonical pathway is activated there, and whether TGF-beta drives that activity. Some SMAD2/3-dependent transcription can persist without SMAD4; SMAD4 independence does not imply that all SMAD signalling is absent. [NC2] [NC5] [NC9] [SM14]

G359E has investigator-reported functional impairment in a TGF-beta reporter assay but retains an overall VUS assessment. It is acquired in the primary tumour; mutant RNA was observed there (251/550 fragments), but not in sampled resection RNA (0/58). [SM1] [SM14]

The later RNA result does not prove DNA-clone loss or connect the resection response to mutant-bearing cells. The assay does not establish complete or biallelic functional loss in current disease, ERK activation or mutation-specific vactosertib benefit.

The ten-gene response set is mixed, while immediate-early signals are strong in the resection. EGFR and other receptor inputs are credible alternatives; SHC1 RNA does not resolve isoforms with different signalling effects.
TGF-beta-to-ERK coupling remains a hypothesis. These data give no new basis to add a MEK/ERK inhibitor or increase its priority merely because ERK machinery is present. [NC1] [NC2] [NC3]

TAK1, p38 and JNK
Stress-response branches

BostonGene MAP3K7/TAK1 is 100th percentile, with total-protein machinery present but mixed. No activating phosphorylation was measured. These pathways also respond to inflammation and cellular stress.

Some experimental TGFBR1-TRAF6-TAK1 routes do not require receptor kinase activity. Their presence therefore does not guarantee suppression by an ALK5 kinase inhibitor; dependency is context-specific. [NC6] [NC7]

PI3K / AKT
Survival and growth signalling

BostonGene AKT2/3 are 91st/100th percentiles. Total AKT1/2 protein rank shifts are +24.99/+22.21 Astral points. Historical PTEN truncation offers a separate mechanism; PTEN RNA abundance does not show retained protein function.
There is no phospho-AKT readout or proof that TGF-beta is the driver. These results do not establish a rationale for empirically adding PI3K/AKT inhibition to the proposed immunotherapy combination.

Rho / ROCK
Cell shape and contractility
BostonGene ROCK1 is 99th percentile; available Rho-pathway proteins are not uniformly raised. GTP loading and kinase activity were not measured.
Expression supports available machinery, not a demonstrated active or drug-dependent branch. It does not provide a new therapeutic ranking signal.
Fibroblasts and immune cells need not share the tumour’s SMAD4 mutation. Their response to TGF-beta can remain relevant even if malignant-cell canonical signalling is impaired.

Vactosertib retains its conditional stromal/immune research rationale. This analysis does not upgrade expected efficacy or establish a G359E-specific treatment match; human SMAD4-stratified benefit has not been demonstrated. [NC8]

SMAD4-deficient CRC experiments support class-level plausibility for other inhibitors, not proof of vactosertib benefit for this allele or current node. [NC3] [NC4] Tempus lists TGFBR1 and EPHB2 as low-DNA-coverage regions, limiting negative genotype interpretation; this says nothing about RNA level or ALK5 target activity. [C5] No new tissue-culture experiments are proposed.

PAGES.title: What other human stromal trials say about biomarker selection
blocks: INCA33890, an antibody targeting PD-1 and TGF-beta receptor 2, provides the most relevant baseline comparison. Among 105 CRC patients, 16 responses were reported (15.2%), including 14 confirmed. Higher PD-L1-positive tissue area and IFNG/CXCL9/CXCL10 or T-cell-inflammatory RNA associated with response/stable disease; TGF-beta RNA/signatures did not. Stromal-rich CMS4 had 1/13 responses versus 5/23 for CMS2. These small exploratory groups do not establish a selection rule. [VT7] [VT15]

INCA33890 IHC included 78 patients and subtype analysis 44; the RNA denominator was not specified. PD-L1 area >5% had 5/13 responses, but this is not an RNA threshold. Blood mutation burden >20 had 5/15 versus 8/64 below 20. Later on-treatment studies included only three patients for phospho-SMAD; large cell counts in spatial plots are not independent patient counts. Neither study validates a case-specific probability. [VT7] [VT8]

One response among 32 pretreated CRC patients (3.1%); median progression-free survival 1.3 months. The sole responder had stromal-rich CMS4 disease and relatively high PD-L1, but no observed TGF-beta activation. [VT9]
One responder cannot validate CMS4 or high TGF-beta as a selector. Related mechanisms can have very different clinical activity.

20 MSS patients (11 CRC, nine pancreatic): zero RECIST responses and 25% stable disease. Fourteen paired biopsies showed immune changes. A baseline cytokine decision tree and response-associated changes were exploratory. [VT10]
High case CXCL12 supports the mechanism, not a likelihood of shrinkage. Tissue immune effects and prolonged stability are different endpoints.

Randomized 55-patient head-and-neck trial selected fibroblast-rich tumours. Primary tumour-size endpoint was negative; response rates 33% versus 32%. Secondary progression-free survival signal: HR 0.58, P = .1023 under a relaxed alpha of .20. [VT11]
Not CRC; no validated fibroblast-by-treatment interaction. Neither fibroblast abundance nor the screening survival signal establishes likely benefit here.

Small preliminary CRC biomarker analyses associated disease control with lower LAIR1 (P = .0142), and a non-significant trend toward more mature collagen (P = .0642). Blood associations also came from small selected groups. [VT12] [VT13]
Not a validated LAIR1-high or collagen-high rule. Bulk matrix RNA and shared LAIR1/2 peptide assignments cannot reproduce these assays.

These studies favour measured human response evidence over a simple 'target high, drug likely effective' rule. INCA33890's October 2026 first-line chemotherapy/bevacizumab combination response rate (71%, n = 42) cannot be applied to this later-line case or isolate the antibody's contribution. No head-to-head study establishes the best stromal agent; none of these biomarker analyses validates post-BOT/BAL rescue. [VT14]

PAGES.title: Therapeutic discussion priorities for recruitment stroma and adenosine
blocks: Within-axis ranks weigh relevant human efficacy, case biology, prior treatment and toxicity. They are discussion priorities, not comparative efficacy estimates. A biologically attractive agent can rank below a regimen with stronger human evidence. Access is stated separately; unavailable agents remain in the same list. Several agents span axes and must not be counted as independent solutions.

1 TGF-beta/checkpoint strategy (vactosertib or INCA33890).
2 CXCL12 blockade with NOX-A12 plus checkpoint therapy.
3 Personalised vaccine plus an immune partner; N-803 as an investigational addition.

TGF-directed combinations have some MSS CRC responses. NOX-A12 has human tissue-trafficking evidence but no objective responses in its small mixed CRC/pancreatic cohort. Vaccine-specific T cells can reach human tumours.

None is selected by low CXCL9/10/11. Prior BOT/BAL limits TGF-trial extrapolation. Vaccination and N-803 primarily address specificity/expansion. Systemic N-803 remains investigational. [VT1] [VT7] [NV1] [L10]

1 Vactosertib + PD-1 or INCA33890 (same exploratory tier).
2 NOX-A12 + PD-1.
3 NOX4 inhibition (setanaxib) or FAP radioligand strategies.
4 CTHRC1 antibody PBP1710; NC410/LAIR; integrin/LOX approaches.

Vactosertib and INCA33890 have direct CRC activity. The 28-sample vactosertib RNA analysis found no significant baseline program association; no stromal selection rule is validated. Later options have weaker CRC outcomes or are preclinical.

On 6 November Dr Kesari said the Asthra team would add me to its vactosertib single-patient IND access list; approval and supply are not confirmed. INCA33890 eligibility gates remain. Setanaxib evidence is non-CRC; PBP1710 is preclinical, NC410 terminated. [VE9] [VT7] [VT8] [VT11] [NV12] [R5] [VR1]

1 Etrumadenant-containing immune/chemotherapy regimen.
2 ENPP1 inhibitor RBS2418.
3 Vizenpistat + BOT/BAL.
4 CD73 or CD39-directed agents.

Etrumadenant has randomized whole-regimen CRC evidence; it does not isolate the adenosine drug. RBS2418 is the more direct ENPP1/cGAMP hypothesis. Later combinations have smaller or weaker efficacy evidence.

Etrumadenant development/access is paused; ranking does not imply availability. Expression is not a validated predictor. RBS2418 data remain early; CD39 can mark useful T cells. Vizenpistat does not validate retreatment after prior BOT/BAL. [L12] [L31] [T13] [L33]

Recruitment and stromal choices overlap; they are not independent solutions. Pembrolizumab is the discussed PD-1 component of the four-part proposal, while BOT/BAL is an alternative requiring renewed clinical/sponsor agreement. No trial validates the complete regimen or an optimal schedule. [VE9]

PAGES.title: Therapeutic discussion priorities for recognition effectors and other axes
blocks:
1 AC484 (ABBV-CLS-484) ± PD-1.
2 APC-derived PTPN13-inhibitory peptide TAT-APC11.
3 Epigenetic/checkpoint approaches.
4 Other PTPN12/PTPN13 approaches.

AC484 inhibits PTPN1/PTPN2 and has a strong preclinical rationale, without validated CRC benefit or a case-selection assay. Epigenetic combinations have mixed human CRC results but a less specific case rationale. APC11 and other phosphatase approaches are preclinical.

AC484 trial/EAP availability requires sponsor confirmation; old registry information does not establish access. TAT-APC11 is preclinical; synthesis is not clinical readiness. Retained bulk HLA proteins do not prove malignant-cell presentation. [L1] [L3] [L5] [L15] [L16] [T11]

1 Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab (whole-regimen evidence).
2 Selective AXL/MERTK/CSF1 strategies.
3 CD47/SIRPalpha strategies.
Zanzalintinib has randomized CRC survival evidence but multiple vascular/kinase effects; this does not prove myeloid causality. Selective approaches have limited CRC efficacy.

Prior PD-1/PD-L1 was excluded from the pivotal zanzalintinib study. BA3011 is an AXL-targeting ADC, distinct from signalling blockade. Indiscriminate myeloid removal could impair antigen presentation. [L13] [L14]

1 Tumour-reactive TCR therapy.
2 Personalised vaccine + immune partner.
3 N-803-supported vaccine/checkpoint.
4-8 DC, delivery and metabolic leads ranked in the vaccine section.
9 Repeat BOT/BAL alone.

TCR and vaccine evidence is stronger than inferred DC rescue. N-803 expands effectors; comparative non-CRC rescue evidence is negative. FLT3L, CD40 and local priming are exploratory; MCT1/GCL remain lower. Repeating BOT/BAL alone adds no demonstrated overcoming mechanism.

Cell therapy has antigen/HLA, eligibility and conditioning gates. Vaccine manufacture is not immunity or natural target display. Systemic N-803 needs appropriate product/route review. New leads remain global tier5, without confirmed CRC access or personal response prediction. [L18] [NV1] [NV10] [NV11] [VE3] [VE4] [VE9]

1 ONO-4578 + nivolumab in an appropriate study.
2 Other selective EP4 agents such as E7046.
3 COX2 inhibition: no established immune-rescue role here.
Low published CRC activity and no PGE2 measurement. PTGS2 RNA alone does not select benefit.
Celecoxib has gastrointestinal, renal and cardiovascular risks; no demonstrated CRC checkpoint rescue here. [L36] [L37]

1 Evidence-based bevacizumab-containing CRC regimen when indicated.
2 Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab.
3 Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab.
Standard CRC benefit is stronger than this case’s hypoxia hypothesis. Zanzalintinib has phase III whole-regimen evidence; LEAP-017 missed its prespecified survival endpoint.
This is not permission to add bevacizumab to current anti-EGFR therapy. Prior therapy, toxicity and regimen-level evidence govern selection. [L13] [L24] [L25] [L34]

1 TTX080 + cetuximab.
2 Monalizumab + durvalumab.
3 TIGIT, galectin or TIM3-directed trial agents.
These remain weak case-specific options: limited CRC activity, unconfirmed relevant cellular engagement; HLA-G gene-specific protein is not established.
TTX080’s anti-EGFR-naive results do not establish benefit after panitumumab. No current access or individual response prediction is established. [L29] [L40]

These rankings concern immunotherapy resistance, not all systemic options. ADCs, chemotherapy, radioligands and local treatment may work through other mechanisms; their separate website ranking is retained. No evidence here establishes failure of the current regimen.

PAGES.title: Stromal abundance does not establish physical exclusion
blocks: Stroma means nonmalignant supporting tissue, including fibroblasts, matrix and vessels. More stroma is not equivalent to more immune suppression. Fibroblasts can restrict, support or reshape tumour immunity, depending on their state and location.
Tempus broad matrix programme; BostonGene median 88th percentile across 32 reported matrix genes; B7 abundant matrix proteins.
Caris FN1 4th percentile; smooth-muscle 11-gene signal extreme in B4 and corroborated by B7 proteins. Normal bowel wall and repair are plausible contributors.
Strong for treated resection; not established across all lesions or times.
B7 selective CTHRC1/FAP/LRRC15/THBS2 enrichment; TGF-associated RNA, CXCL12 and latent-activation machinery.
CTHRC1/LRRC15 BostonGene 47th/43rd; broad protein TGF signatures near reference centre. No cell-specific signalling or secreted active ligand measurement.
Moderate support for a CAF-state hypothesis; suppressive function and specific subtype unresolved.
Gut/other CRC literature provides a credible mechanism; BostonGene reports fibrotic, immune non-inflamed tissue.
No spatial CD8 intranest-to-stromal ratio or collagen orientation measurement. Low recruitment-ligand RNA is also compatible with an immune-poor state.
Not directly measured. Bulk expression cannot establish a barrier.
Selective stromal mechanisms are biologically plausible, and clinical studies show activity in some patients.
No current-node RNA/proteome/spatial panel or functional rescue. Historical liver and rectum differ; prior BOT/BAL resistance may have several causes.
Unproven; archival expression cannot establish current treatment dependence.
Confidence decreases down this table. Many pathways share the same genes and the same archival specimen; they must not be counted as independent confirmations. [D1] [D2] [S18] [S19]

PAGES.title: Support and counterevidence across datasets
blocks: TGF receptor/Hallmark machinery; ITGB6 72nd CRC percentile. Raw-read research estimates available for all panel genes.
