Clinical FN1 4th, VEGFA 6th, KDR 36th and TGFBI 36th. CAF/ECM and fibroblast TGF-response modules are near or below external reference middle. TGFBI is not TGFB1.
Broad matrix, TGF-associated responses, CXCL12; most findings persist after coding-transcript sensitivity.
All 11 smooth-muscle genes above reference upper quartile; normal-stroma ECM-down high too. Some total gene estimates are noncoding-sensitive. Research values are not clinical percentiles.
CXCL12 99th; TGFB2/3 98th; TGFBR1/2 99th. Portrait: fibrotic, immune non-inflamed.
Smooth-muscle median 100th, epithelial median 1st. CTHRC1 47th, LRRC15 43rd, TGFBI 8th; minimal active infiltration can mean poor recruitment. Same block as Tempus, not an independent lesion.
Selective CAF proteins, THBS2/ITGA5 and LOX/LOXL1 have multi-peptide support; four descriptive reference comparisons.
One proteome with duplicate exports, different block from B4; strong muscle/repair. No phosphoproteome, activity assay or current-node protein evidence.
Selected single-cell data place FAP/LRRC15 in fibroblast subsets; GARP and ITGB6 provide compartment clues.
Only 101 selected genes, no full cell matrix; CTHRC1 omitted. Liver bulk sequencing failed QC. No spatial geometry or full pathway scoring possible.
Matrix/contractile values in merged export retained gene by gene.
Specimen/pipeline/reference linkage unresolved; cannot call this independent liver validation or convert to GSE percentiles.
Both cell-free and buffy-coat measurements retained in the full gene matrix.
Blood RNA is not lesion RNA; both contain stromal-associated transcripts but cannot establish a tumour CAF state.
Reports stromal enrichment and a high smooth-muscle background score.
Input/normalisation unresolved; strongly divergent purity estimates. Derived analysis is not a new independent assay.
Histology confirms carcinoma in A2, with very focal lymphoid tissue. No current-node RNA/proteome has been located.
No current-node expression/proteome located. A1 necrosis and limited sampling complicate immune interpretation; no exclusion map.

Original-source review and all 236 public catalogue records checked; no further case-specific molecular delivery found in the targeted recent correspondence search. “All” refers to located data, not unprovided laboratory holdings. [D1] [D2] [D3] [C16]

PAGES.title: How the pathway comparison was performed
blocks: The analysis uses the completed Caris and Tempus native-read Salmon 2.8.0 quantifications with the same GENCODE v37 transcript index as 18 GSE50760 primary colorectal tumours. The present revision re-extracts all genes and scores pathways; it does not rerun sequencing or claim a clinical assay. GSE50760 contains stage IV primary tumours, including one MSI-high case, and differs in library preparation, treatment and tissue composition. [Q7] [Q8] [Q3]
How to read the next tables
Unweighted mean of log2(TPM + 1) across a set, avoiding domination by the largest collagen count.
M = number of 18 reference samples with a lower set mean. 18/18 means higher than these 18, not a clinical 100th percentile.
Each gene ranked in a fixed 19,619 coding-gene universe; gene ranks averaged.
R = reference samples with a lower average rank. Substantial M/R disagreement flags transcriptome-composition sensitivity.
Only protein-coding transcript contributions retained, keeping the original whole-transcriptome TPM denominator.
C = reference samples lower on the coding mean-log measure. This is not re-normalisation or a vendor-matched percentile.
Median of individually reported colorectal gene percentiles; missing genes excluded and coverage shown.
A median of percentiles is descriptive, not a validated pathway percentile. Caris has too few clinical panel genes for comparable module scores.
Median per-gene B7-minus-reference rank shift among eligible common proteins; strict assignment and reference coverage applied.
Δ = descriptive shift in rank points; n = eligible genes. Different protein and RNA coverage means the scores are not interchangeable.
Exact Dominguez 11, rectal matrix-CAF 13, C-ECM up/down and Pan-F-TBRS memberships plus official Hallmarks; additional curated mechanism panels.
Mixed ligand/receptor/inhibitor panels inventory components. Even directional response signatures do not prove pathway activation or cell source.

37 overlapping sets plus target review / 1,225 unique genes; 83,187-gene source union. Leave-one-gene-out, reference coverage, coding and rank sensitivities are saved. No enrichment p-values, validated CMS4 classification or reconstructed Gut classifier are asserted. Pan-F-TBRS membership is corroborated by author-associated/public sources; original Nature table S8 was not directly retrieved. Calon’s original 165-gene classifier was not reconstructed. [D1] [D2] [S5] [S25] [S4]

PAGES.title: All pathway results 1 of 2
blocks: Caris and Tempus: M/R/C = reference samples lower out of 18 by total mean-log / within-sample rank / coding mean-log. Higher counts indicate relative abundance, not functional activation. BostonGene and B7 parentheses show gene coverage.

No pathway-level estimate is valid for the selected liver export, unresolved Valius bulk provenance or tumour attribution of blood RNA. Those sources are displayed separately, not silently excluded or scored as zero. Full per-gene and per-reference results accompany this report. [D1] [D2]

PAGES.title: All pathway results 2 of 2
blocks: Caris and Tempus: M/R/C = reference samples lower out of 18 by total mean-log / within-sample rank / coding mean-log. Higher counts indicate relative abundance, not functional activation. BostonGene and B7 parentheses show gene coverage.

No pathway-level estimate is valid for the selected liver export, unresolved Valius bulk provenance or tumour attribution of blood RNA. Those sources are displayed separately, not silently excluded or scored as zero. Full per-gene and per-reference results accompany this report. [D1] [D2]

PAGES.title: RNA pathway contrasts across all 18 references
blocks: Each grey dot is one GSE50760 primary tumour; coloured marks are the two archival patient samples. The fixed-universe within-sample ranks expose composition-sensitive differences that TPM means can obscure. Gene sets overlap; this is descriptive, not a clinical classifier. [D1]

Tempus broad matrix and smooth muscle remain strong on the rank measure; its specific CAF signal is less extreme. Both samples have low CXCR3 recruitment ligands. Matrix composition and immune recruitment therefore remain distinct, potentially cooperating explanations.

PAGES.title: TGF beta ligands and pathway activity
blocks: TPM = research transcripts per million; total/coding estimates share a whole-transcriptome denominator. Caris/BostonGene percentiles are separately assay-matched. NS in the Caris column = percentile not supplied by Caris, not absent RNA or assay failure. B7 shows source-labelled unique peptides/descriptive Astral rank shift, not a clinical percentile or fold change. NR elsewhere = not reported/assigned/eligible. [C4] [C15] [D1] [D2]

The resection has coherent ligand/receptor and selected response RNA, but the early biopsy is less consistent: coding-only TGFB1 is near the external median (10.69 versus 10.53 TPM). TGFB2/3 remain high in Tempus coding comparisons. TGFBI is below the median in both provider panels (Caris 36th; BostonGene 8th). Receptors and feedback genes can be present without active signalling; nuclear pSMAD2/3, active-versus-total TGF-beta and cell localisation are the missing measurements. [D1]

Activin is a competing TGF-beta-family signal: INHBA total RNA is 60.8 / 20.7 TPM (Caris / Tempus), BostonGene 73rd percentile; ALK4/ACVR1B is 14th and ACVR2A 97th. Antagonists FST/FSTL3 are 94th/98th. These mixed components do not establish active activin, but pSMAD2/3 or ALK4/5-inhibitor rescue alone cannot distinguish it from TGF-beta. [D1] [D12] [D13]

TGFB1 protein has two latent-associated-peptide-region and two mature-chain peptides. Mature-region detection does not establish release of active ligand. LTBP2, included in the broader panel, does not directly bind latent TGF-beta. Total integrin subunits do not demonstrate an active alpha-v/beta-8 heterodimer. [D2] [S29]

PAGES.title: Matrix composition and mechanical signalling
blocks: TPM = research transcripts per million; total/coding estimates share a whole-transcriptome denominator. Caris/BostonGene percentiles are separately assay-matched. NS in the Caris column = percentile not supplied by Caris, not absent RNA or assay failure. B7 shows source-labelled unique peptides/descriptive Astral rank shift, not a clinical percentile or fold change. NR elsewhere = not reported/assigned/eligible. [C4] [C15] [D1] [D2]

ITGA5, THBS2, LOX and LOXL1 are stronger convergent protein leads than DDR1 or a specific GPR4-LOXL2 route. FN1’s large research TPM difference is not a validated longitudinal fold change. Caris’s assay-matched 4th percentile directly argues against a uniformly fibronectin-high early biopsy. FAK/YAP total abundance does not measure phosphorylation, nuclear localisation or force transmission. [D1] [D2]

Collagen orientation, pore structure, stiffness and crosslink chemistry were not measured. LOX precursor/mature peptides do not establish enzyme activity. Total FAK/YAP is not activated FAK or nuclear YAP; different LOX-family genes and inhibitors are not interchangeable. [D1] [D2] [S13] [S12] [S14] [S15]

PAGES.title: Fibroblast states and myeloid communication
blocks: TPM = research transcripts per million; total/coding estimates share a whole-transcriptome denominator. Caris/BostonGene percentiles are separately assay-matched. NS in the Caris column = percentile not supplied by Caris, not absent RNA or assay failure. B7 shows source-labelled unique peptides/descriptive Astral rank shift, not a clinical percentile or fold change. NR elsewhere = not reported/assigned/eligible. [C4] [C15] [D1] [D2]

Specific CAF markers are not uniformly high in RNA: BostonGene places CTHRC1/LRRC15 near its median, while B7 supports both proteins. Its phenotype could include several fibroblast states rather than a single dominant subtype. SPP1 may originate from tumour cells or myeloid cells; bulk abundance cannot choose between published SPP1-CAF mechanisms. IL6/STAT3 sets are rank-sensitive and LIF is low in BostonGene. [D1] [D2]

In the BostonGene portrait, fibroblasts 20.47%, endothelium 1.91%, CD8 PD1-low 0.94% and PD1-high <0.5% are RNA-inferred estimates, not histological counts. The report’s “fibrotic, immune non-inflamed” category supports stromal/immune-poor tissue but does not establish where the few T cells sit. [C3]

PAGES.title: Recruitment and vascular alternatives
blocks: TPM = research transcripts per million; total/coding estimates share a whole-transcriptome denominator. Caris/BostonGene percentiles are separately assay-matched. NS in the Caris column = percentile not supplied by Caris, not absent RNA or assay failure. B7 shows source-labelled unique peptides/descriptive Astral rank shift, not a clinical percentile or fold change. NR elsewhere = not reported/assigned/eligible. [C4] [C15] [D1] [D2]

CXCL9/10/11 are all below the external reference first quartile in both research RNA samples. Estimated supporting fragments are sparse: Caris 5/4/0; Tempus 23/8/4. BostonGene CXCL10 3rd percentile corroborates low recruitment-ligand RNA, while CXCL9 is 28th. Low ligand RNA could cause poor entry, or result from too few activated T cells and weak interferon feedback; it does not identify direction of causality. [D1]

VEGFA clinical percentiles are low in both providers. The hypoxia Hallmark changes substantially between mean-log and rank methods in Caris (13 versus 0 references lower), whereas Tempus is more stable (18 versus 17); HIF1A transcript does not measure oxygen or protein stabilisation. Vascular suppression needs vessel-specific activation/perfusion and endothelial Fas-ligand localisation, not endothelial abundance alone. [S17] [S10]

PAGES.title: Liver and blood evidence and unresolved sources
blocks: 92,897 recovered cells, 16 labels; only 101 selected genes. Fibroblast label: 16,040 cells; CD8: 2,231; macrophages: 11,273.
Recovered-cell proportions are affected by sampling/dissociation. No spatial barrier or full CAF response signature can be reconstructed.
FAP RNA detected in 3.91% and LRRC15 in 0.89% of labelled fibroblasts.
Provides cell-source clues, not protein positivity or proof these rare detected subsets dominate suppression. Dropout/selection unresolved. CTHRC1 is omitted, not zero.
LRRC32/GARP detected in 29.26% of fibroblasts and 28.25% of endothelial cells. ITGB6 in 20.72% of other tumour cells and 8.54% of partial-EMT tumour cells.
Identifies candidate compartments, but aggregates cannot establish coexpression, active heterodimers or signalling.
FN1 detected in 32.96% of fibroblasts and 55.37% of hepatocytes. CA9 in 38.25% of partial-EMT tumour cells.
Fibronectin is not CAF-exclusive. CA9 is a historical hypoxia-associated clue, not a direct oxygen measure or evidence about the current node.
Two blood fractions, not extra tumour biopsies. Tissue origin, dilution and library composition prevent lesion-specific stromal interpretation. All panel genes retained in source matrix.
Reported log2(TPM+1): CTHRC1 6.2; LRRC15 3.6; FN1 11.6; CXCL12 8.0.
Specimen and pipeline linkage unresolved; these are not converted to patient-specific CRC percentiles or assigned to the liver.
Reports 8.29-fold stromal enrichment versus TCGA READ; smooth-muscle score 0.815; nominal 45% tumour / 30% stroma / 25% immune.
Purity methods range 10-55%, adopted estimate 45% with 26-71% range. Input/normalisation unresolved; not a measured cell fraction or independent assay.
Reports hypoxia 7-gene score 3.21-fold and interferon 10-gene score 1.39-fold.
Cannot equate these secondary scores with biochemical hypoxia, pathway activation or the independently recalculated Hallmarks.
All selected liver, blood and unresolved bulk values are retained in the analysis. The limited liver export cannot establish a full pathway signature or spatial mechanism. [C6] [C12] [C7] [D1] [D3]

PAGES.title: Selective CAF protein signals and broader matrix patterns
blocks: Median B7-minus-reference rank shift in points; parentheses = eligible genes. Strict common-protein comparisons, not fold changes, clinical percentiles or repeated patient specimens.

The Astral CAF-remodelling and published CAF11 panels shift more than broad matrix. However, the Hallmark TGF and fibroblast TGF-response protein summaries are close to the reference centre, and matrix maturation is mixed. Thus the protein evidence supports selective fibroblast-associated proteins more strongly than universal activation of every fibrotic pathway. Available-gene and reference-coverage sensitivities are saved in full. [D2]

One treated B7 proteome underlies all these comparisons. External CPTAC paired tumour/normal statistics describe that cohort, not a patient-matched difference. Public iBAQ values cannot be directly divided into the patient’s arbitrary-unit intensities. Each reference retains a different protein set; medians are not interchangeable tumour-versus-normal contrasts. Preparation, tissue composition and missingness remain limitations.

PAGES.title: Protein specificity and limits of interpretation
blocks: 2,237,260 arbitrary units; rank 664 of 7,706 detected proteins. Five source-labelled sequences; three conservative I/L-aware substring-specific, five fully tryptic-specific in reviewed human isoforms.
A within-proteome signal rank is not a CRC percentile. Bulk mass spectrometry does not localise CTHRC1 to a fibroblast or tumour boundary.
Are CAF markers merely more matrix?
CTHRC1/FAP/LRRC15 relative to the geometric mean of seven broad matrix markers: +2.01/+1.11/+2.10 log2-ratio differences versus Astral median.
These descriptive cross-study ratios suggest selectivity but do not adjust for cell fractions or provide validated fold changes.
Against DES/CNN1/MYH11/TAGLN instead, the same differences are −0.81/−1.70/−1.13. Strong multi-peptide muscle proteins corroborate the RNA.
Bowel wall, pericytes and myofibroblasts overlap markers. High ACTG2 has only one vendor-unique peptide; stronger muscle markers, not ACTG2 alone, support this concern.
TGFB1 four unique sequences; LTBP1/2/4 10/13/8; GARP five; thrombospondin-1 23; ITGAV 36.
TGFB1 fragments do not measure active released ligand. LTBP2 is contextual, not a direct latent-ligand binder; beta6/beta8 unassigned is not absence.
ITGA5 23, LOX 3, LOXL1 10, FAK 15, YAP1 7 source-labelled unique sequences. LOX includes propeptide and mature regions.
No crosslink chemistry, LOX enzyme flux, pFAK or nuclear YAP measured. LOXL2/NOX4 not assigned. FAK coding RNA is less extreme than total RNA.
LAIR1/LAIR2 appear as one shared group, 65,397 AU, zero source-labelled unique sequences.
This is not independent confirmation of either receptor. Surface LAIR1 on the relevant immune compartment and receptor-dependent suppression remain unmeasured.

Peptide audit: 278 sequences across 35 key proteins, against 42,545 reviewed-human protein sequence records, including canonical proteins and annotated isoforms, with isoleucine/leucine and enzyme-compatible specificity distinguished. No raw spectral re-search or phosphoproteomics was available. [D2]

PAGES.title: What colorectal mechanism studies add to the inference
blocks: Tauriello: TGF blockade restored immune control and checkpoint sensitivity in MSS-like CRC liver models. New spatial ALK5 work shifted fibroblast/immune niches without reducing tumour size. [S1] [S22]

TGF-associated RNA supports biological plausibility, not a response predictor. Microenvironment changes without tumour shrinkage show why pharmacodynamic effects must be separated from clinical efficacy.

Fibroblast thrombospondin-2 at the invasive front suppressed myeloid CXCL9/10; genetic deletion restored CD8 entry. CXCR3/ligand blockade reversed rescue; dendritic-cell depletion abolished tumour-control benefit. Checkpoint blockade addressed residual exhaustion. [S11]
THBS2 has 17 B7 peptides and +37.3 rank points; low recruitment ligands fit the published mechanism. Cell source and causality are unmeasured. No established clinical THBS2 inhibitor is identified.
Tumour SPP1 signalled through CAF CD44, beta-catenin/HIF1alpha and CXCL12; blockade improved immunotherapy response. Some experimental systems are not MSS-like. [S10]
SPP1 is detected and CXCL12 is high in B4. The case does not establish tumour versus macrophage SPP1 or HIF1alpha protein stabilisation.
CRC work separates impaired peripheral memory-CD8 recruitment from SPP1-macrophage restraint of intratumoural expansion. Human FAP-SPP1 spatial association is complementary. [S9] [S8]
Recruitment and intratumoural expansion can be separately impaired. Bulk FAP/SPP1 cannot diagnose the niche; Qi’s ICI validation used bladder, not CRC.
Fibroblast alpha5-integrin supported fibronectin/collagen deposition; targeting it potentiated PD-L1 blockade in preclinical CRC. [S13]
ITGA5 has convergent RNA/protein evidence and is a stronger case-specific matrix lead than several alternatives. Human CRC therapeutic efficacy is not established.
DDR1 extracellular supermeres altered fibroblast contraction/alignment; experimental PRTH101 did not inhibit contraction. GPR4 acted through LOXL2 in colon models. [S12] [S14]
DDR1 is relatively low; GPR4 RNA and LOXL2 protein offer weaker support. A genetic model effect does not establish antibody efficacy.
These studies establish mechanisms in defined models; none prospectively predicts benefit for this patient from bulk expression alone.

PAGES.title: CTHRC1 and fibroblast signatures in the literature
blocks: The Gut study’s most relevant result is the association between CTHRC1-positive stroma and a low ratio of CD8 cells inside tumour epithelium versus surrounding stroma. Galunisertib changed this phenotype in a mouse liver-metastasis model, but direct CTHRC1 inhibition was not tested. The MSS checkpoint analysis involved 15 localised NICHE cases; H-score 175 came from 23 metastatic MSI cases. These cohorts do not establish a validated cutoff or likely benefit in metastatic MSS disease after BOT/BAL. [R2]
Dominguez defines an exact activated-myofibroblast set; pancreatic LRRC15-cell depletion supports causality in that setting. [S5] [S6]
Pancreatic CAF depletion is not proof that inhibiting LRRC15 protein or targeting a near-median RNA marker will help this case.
Mariathasan links a fibroblast signature to checkpoint resistance, particularly the immune-excluded phenotype. [S4]
The human treatment cohort was urothelial. Contractile genes overlap smooth muscle, and a high bulk score is not a CRC drug-selection assay.
Published up/down sets help distinguish altered CAF matrix from normal stromal programmes. [S25]
Do not combine up/down as one suppressive score. Tempus has both up and down high, highlighting tissue composition. Non-CRC immunotherapy cohorts limit prediction.
Human CRC stromal programmes can explain poor-prognosis transcriptomic subtypes. CAF IL11-GP130/STAT3 supports metastatic seeding. [S3] [S2]
Bulk “EMT” does not prove epithelial conversion. Metastatic growth support is distinct from T-cell exclusion. No validated CMS4 call is made here.
Human lung live imaging shows fibre organisation guides T-cell migration; vascular Fas-ligand can create a selective barrier. [S15] [S17]
Neither matrix amount nor endothelial-marker expression substitutes for patient geometry, perfusion or endothelial-specific Fas-ligand.

The case has CTHRC1 protein and RNA, but no comparable spatial score or clinical-response biomarker. PBP1710 remains preclinical, with sponsor-planned H2 2027 entry; neither target presence nor its development establishes likely efficacy. [R3] [R5] [R6]

PAGES.title: Competing explanations constrain the conclusions
blocks: Evidence here and in the literature
B4 smooth-muscle median 100th provider percentile, epithelial median 1st; strong B7 MYH11/CNN1/DES/TAGLN. Resection includes deeper tissue than biopsy.
A major confounder for high matrix/contractile scores; no reliable cell-fraction adjustment is available. Evidence for more tissue stroma is stronger than evidence for a suppressive CAF state.
The resection followed therapy. Rectal paired studies find persistent matrix CAF/NF-kappaB states with poor response; platinum retention can induce CAF programmes. [S20] [S21]
A plausible explanation for biopsy/resection differences, but different samples, treatment and assays prevent attributing the change to therapy or tumour evolution.

Both samples have low CXCR3 ligands; BostonGene non-inflamed portrait and low inferred active CD8. THBS2 offers one suppressive explanation, but lack of antigen recognition can also reduce interferon feedback.
Low chemokines and few active T cells support this alternative. The available data cannot distinguish cause from deficient interferon feedback after failed recognition.
CAF IL11/STAT3 or matrix signals may support survival independently of exclusion. Spatial ALK5 treatment can change microenvironment without size benefit. [S2] [S22]
Stroma may support growth independently of immunity. Altering a CAF signature or immune-cell ratio is not equivalent to tumour response.
Broad alphaSMA-fibroblast depletion worsened CRC in a model, reducing BMP4 and increasing TGF-beta/Tregs. Putative protective mucosal CAF states also exist. [S18] [S19]
Selective CAF markers cannot justify broad fibroblast depletion. Protective and suppressive states may coexist, and removal can have adverse effects in models.
Current node has a different bottleneck
Most evidence is from October 2024 rectum/liver; node histology alone cannot carry those mechanisms forward.
The current dominant resistance mechanism remains uncertain. Historical rectum/liver data support hypotheses, not a diagnosis of present nodal resistance.
These alternatives can coexist. The evidence does not support treating “fibrosis”, “EMT”, “hypoxia” or “CTHRC1-positive” as interchangeable diagnoses. [S23] [S24]

PAGES.title: Reconciling the RNA results
blocks: For the archival biopsy, Caris now supplies the most relevant available expression comparator: its own colorectal assay cohort. Four genes lie around the median, while HLA-C is below the median but not in the extreme lower tail. This supersedes the earlier report's inference that the biopsy independently confirms globally low antigen-presentation expression. [C15]

The previous analysis quantified Caris, Tempus and18 GSE50760 primary colorectal tumours with Salmon2.8.0 and GENCODE 37. TAP1 and HLA-A/B/C were low relative to that small external series. Those numerical comparisons remain reproducible, but identical software cannot eliminate differences in tissue preservation, RNA enrichment, fragment quality, cell mixture or cohort selection. GSE50760 used poly-A-selected RNA; the assay-matched Caris comparison has much greater relevance for interpreting the Caris biopsy. Neither comparator validates a tumour-cell-specific biological defect. [Q7] [Q8] [Q3]

The new table uses58,610 comparator cases; the provider narrative says59,608. That unresolved count discrepancy does not explain away the near-median percentile values. Both source values are retained. Caris states30% tumour and QC passed. Provider total TPM differs from our research TPM, especially for IRF1 and HLA-A, so they are not interchangeable measurements. [C15]
Coding RNA and cell composition remain important

Caris reports protein-coding shares of11% for IRF1 and21% for TAP1, versus97%,85% and67% for HLA-A/B/C. These are transcript annotation categories, not translated protein fractions or measurements of abnormal splicing. There is no coding-only assay-matched cohort distribution. TAP1 coding estimates disagree: provider4.07TPM/21% versus earlier research12.71TPM/about68% on the same Caris RNA. IRF1 coding estimates agree more closely at19.3 versus18.8TPM. Transcript-reference/assignment differences require reconciliation before biological interpretation. Do not compare coding TPM against a total-RNA reference or infer a functional loss from the fraction alone. [C15]

BostonGene low IRF1/TAP/HLA and immunoproteasome RNA remains a coherent observation in treated B4 tissue. Low purity and stromal abundance are competing explanations; current evidence cannot distinguish dilution, lack of interferon stimulation, intrinsic repression or subclonal loss. Tempus is useful corroboration from the resection but not an independent longitudinal lesion replicate. No new Tempus assay-matched percentile delivery was found. [C2] [C13] [C14]

Caris percentiles cover a targeted panel: 84 clinical genes plus IRF1, TAP1 and HLA-A/B/C supplied on 7 November. A Caris-column NS means that no assay-matched percentile was supplied; it does not mean the RNA was unmeasured. [C4] [C15]

PAGES.title: Protein evidence and its limits
blocks: Fresh extraction checks the immune-axis table against the supplied patient protein-group matrix. It is a reanalysis of processed quantities and precursor support, not a new search of instrument spectra. The listed intensity is an arbitrary instrument-derived quantity; it cannot be compared between proteins as a molecule count. [P1] [P2]
5 tryptic / 3 conservative specific peptides; see focused audit

NT5E encodes CD73; ENTPD1 encodes CD39. These labels describe the same proteins. Counts are distinct sequences labelled proteotypic in the source, not independently guaranteed gene specificity. In the conservative audit, HLA-C retains3/4 and TAP1 7/8 gene-specific sequences; HLA-A/B, B2M, TAP2, STAT1 and PTPN1/2 retain their specificity; HLA-G does not. The database is not personalised for all patient HLA alleles. The sole HLA-G-labelled sequence DYLALNEDLR is not gene-specific under the I/L-aware audit; HLA-G requires independent confirmation.

The external HPA normal-colon control and unknown run423 are excluded as patient matched normals. Cross-cohort rank shifts are descriptive, not assay-matched CRC percentiles or replicated differential expression. B7 has no measured malignant-cell fraction; bulk HLA can arise from tumour or nonmalignant cells. No phosphoproteomics, surface proteomics or tumour immunopeptidomics was supplied. [P1]

IRF1 and PTPN13 non-detection does not establish absence. High support for STAT1 does not establish STAT1 phosphorylation. The smooth-muscle programme is represented by other contractile proteins even when ACTA2 is not separately assigned. These distinctions prevent protein presence/absence from being turned into a pathway diagnosis.

PAGES.title: Antigen display and phosphatase hypotheses
blocks: Expression supports a mechanism but does not select an AC484 responder

PTPN1 and PTPN2 proteins are detected; BostonGene RNA is 75th and 37th percentile. AC484 inhibits both and can strengthen interferon/immune activity in preclinical models. Early human evidence is mainly renal cancer, not a validated MSS CRC response marker. Neither target expression nor the current mutation data establishes that phosphatase inhibition will overcome this patient’s resistance. [L1] [L2] [C2] [P1]
A fixed antigen display defect is not established

Caris assay-matched IRF1/TAP1/HLA-A/B percentiles are near median, whereas treated B4 RNA is low. Bulk B7 HLA/B2M/TAP proteins remain detectable. This combination is compatible with sampling/composition, weak interferon stimulation or reversible repression; it does not establish tumour-cell surface competence, but argues against assuming complete pathway absence. [C15] [P1]

B2M encodes beta-2-microglobulin, needed for stable HLA class I. The previously discussed cysteine-to-arginine change at residue 100 is a weak, read-end-biased research candidate, not a validated mutation or therapeutic target. No established biallelic B2M loss or disabling JAK/interferon-receptor lesion selects an irreversible mechanism.
APC and PTEN provide distinct preclinical rationales

APC truncations may remove a region that restrains PTPN13. APC11 is an 11-amino-acid APC-derived peptide, with TAT used as a cell-entry tag. Its evidence remains preclinical; PTPN13 RNA is high but its B7 protein is unassigned. AC484 is a different-target intervention. PTEN truncation and NRF2-related RNA offer another route to HLA degradation, but mixed downstream RNA and absent activity/localisation measurements prevent diagnosing that route. [L3] [L4]

PTPN12 protein is present, but the proposed TRIM28/double-stranded-RNA mechanism is unmeasured. Doxycycline in the cited PTPN12 study activated an engineered silencing construct; it was not a PTPN12 inhibitor. Epigenetic combinations have mixed CRC results, with no validated case-specific selector. [L5] [L15] [L16]

A neoantigen vaccine cannot bypass absence of its antigen-HLA target. Conversely, the present data do not establish such absence, so antigen-display uncertainty is a limit on expected efficacy rather than a reason to declare vaccine futility.

PAGES.title: Adenosine and ENPP1 evidence versus clinical efficacy
blocks: CD39 converts ATP/ADP towards AMP; CD73 converts AMP to adenosine, which can suppress immune cells. Both proteins are supported in B7. CD39 can also mark useful tumour-reactive T cells, so its presence is not a simple suppressive-cell count. ENPP1 can reduce extracellular cGAMP/STING signalling and contribute AMP. It has 11 independently checked gene-specific peptides; STING1/TBK1/IRF3 proteins are present, while cGAS protein is unassigned. No metabolite flux or current cellular localisation was measured. [P2] [L11] [L32]
Etrumadenant combination improved outcomes in ARC-9, but included other active agents; the trial does not isolate receptor blockade or validate this expression profile. [L12]
Stronger human CRC support than expression alone, but no demonstrated adenosine dependence in this tumour.
Randomized COLUMBIA1 oleclumab/durvalumab/chemotherapy/bevacizumab did not improve PFS/OS. [L33]
CD73 protein detection is insufficient to infer benefit or justify adding the drug empirically.

Sponsor phase I update: 19 CRC subjects, 17 MSS; 15 biomarker-positive CRC patients had reported median OS 14 months with mixed regimens and no randomized comparator. VISTA-1 is testing efficacy by biomarker strata. [L31] [T16]
B7 ENPP1 and separate bulk cGAS RNA do not equal the trial’s central assay or current-node coexpression. No personal survival or response estimate follows.
NCT06589440 excludes prior PD1/PDL1 or CTLA4 therapy. [T13]
Reported prior BOT/BAL is a direct protocol obstacle; trial existence is not evidence that repeating the combination would work.

VISTA-1 and the phase I RBS2418 study are possible prescreen discussions, not confirmed access or eligibility. Current-regimen failure must not be assumed; actual progression, standard-treatment history and study criteria remain clinical gates. [T12] [T16] [C18]

blocks: AXL 99th, MERTK 93rd, GAS6 80th, CSF1 91st; AXL/CD163/MRC1 proteins. SPP1 RNA 60th and two peptides; TREM2 53rd, protein unassigned.

Broad clearance/myeloid biology is plausible; a dominant suppressive niche is not shown. CSF1R pembrolizumab: 2/41 pMMR CRC responses; CXCR2 navarixin pembrolizumab: 1/40 MSS CRC, futility closure. [L27] [L28]

PTGS2 95th, PTGER4 66th; proteins unassigned; no PGE2 measurement.

VEGFA low provider percentiles; mixed endothelial/hypoxia signals and no perfusion/oxygen evidence.

Established bevacizumab-containing CRC regimens have evidence independent of this hypothesis. Lenvatinib/pembrolizumab failed the prespecified OS endpoint; concurrent EGFR/VEGF additions are not automatically beneficial. [L24] [L25] [L34]
HLA-E supported; HLA-G peptide shared and unconfirmed; other ligands lack matched receptor/activity evidence.
Monalizumab/durvalumab 3/39 response-evaluable MSS CRC; TTX080/cetuximab uncontrolled anti-EGFR-naive signals. Prior treatment and unconfirmed ligand status limit case extrapolation. [L29] [L40]

Complement, glycolysis and tryptophan metabolism remain secondary hypotheses. Abundant LDHA is not selectively high against CRC references, and no lactate, oxygen or kynurenine measurement establishes a dominant metabolic block. Broad JAK inhibition could suppress interferon-mediated immunity rather than restore it. [D1] [D2]
These human results carry more weight for expected efficacy than target detection alone. They do not identify one universally best immunotherapy strategy for this case.

PAGES.title: Conclusions supported by the available evidence
blocks: Poor recruitment is a credible component of resistance

Low CXCR3-ligand RNA, the non-inflamed resection portrait and lower T-cell-lineage signals support an immune-poor state. Stromal and myeloid mechanisms could contribute, but insufficient priming, effector supply or tumour recognition could produce the same weak interferon-chemokine feedback. The data do not resolve which is upstream.
Vaccines and N803 address complementary but incomplete steps

A peptide vaccine can prime useful T cells and N-803 can support responsive NK/CD8 cells. The reviewed vaccine design adds explicit attention to DC antigen delivery, coordinated CD4 help, native tumour recognition and clonal coverage. Intended Hiltonol is already part of the plan. FLT3L and CD40 are distinct DC-support hypotheses; local priming refinements, MCT1 and GCL/BSO remain less established additions, not validated rescue treatments. [VE1] [VE9]
Vactosertib is an investigational possibility rather than a biomarker selected likely success

Its combination trial shows some CRC responses, particularly in an unplanned no-liver-metastasis subgroup. Our complete trial RNA analysis found no significant baseline association across four fixed programs (all primary q = .521). This provides no positive high-stroma selection marker, but does not rule out benefit. [VR1] The available case expression profile is not a validated predictor, the paired IHC subset contained no objective responders, and prior checkpoint-treated patients were excluded. High TGF-associated or stromal expression alone does not justify describing benefit as likely. [L8] [N1] The Monash G359E result materially strengthens evidence of impaired SMAD4-dependent signalling, while the overall clinical classification remains VUS. It does not demonstrate TGF-beta-driven ERK activation in this tumour or increased vactosertib sensitivity. Therapeutic priorities remain unchanged. [SM14] [NC9]
Clinical decisions remain conditional on the disease course

The concrete proposal through Dr Kesari/Asthra is peptide vaccine + vactosertib + N-803 + checkpoint blockade. Pembrolizumab was discussed; BOT/BAL is an alternative after new justification and approval. Vaccine/N-803 access discussions and a vactosertib access-list route do not establish final supply, treatment start or a safe schedule. Current-regimen failure is not established; disease control and current clinical status remain central. [VE9] [C18]

Low-volume active metastatic disease is not the same as disease-free postoperative MRD. Blood immune responses, even broad ones, are not a validated surrogate for tumour control. No new tissue allocation or culture programme is implied. [VE1] [NV2] [NV9]

PAGES.title: Methods data coverage and interpretation limits
blocks: This report integrates archival RNA and protein expression, clinical sequencing, published human treatment evidence and mechanistic literature. The SMAD4 and noncanonical analyses use existing case data, supplemented by an attributed Monash investigator report of the exact G359E functional result on 17 November 2026. Full-universe rank sensitivities, coding contributions, provider-percentile coverage and four external protein comparisons remain available. Modules are descriptive, overlapping and not clinical response scores. Public package reproduction distinguishes downstream recalculation from upstream raw-read/spectral processing.

Caris assay-matched IRF1/TAP1/HLA-A/B results are near median, so the early biopsy does not independently establish globally low antigen display. Caris’s original 36th-percentile item was TGFBI, not the TGFB1 ligand. B7 proteins are from the treated October 2024 rectal resection, not the current node. B2M cysteine-100-to-arginine remains unvalidated; HLA-G remains unsupported by a gene-specific peptide. Prior assumed RECIST nonmeasurability is superseded by the user-reported clinician assessment. [C15] [C4] [P1]

PTPN1/2, PTPN12 and PTPN13 are different targets. Doxycycline was a genetic-switch reagent in the PTPN12 study, not an inhibitor. pSMAD2/3 is shared with activin; vactosertib has ALK4 as well as ALK5 activity. Pharmacodynamic immune shifts do not by themselves predict tumour response. [L1] [L3] [L5] [D12] [D13] [N1]

Full messages and contact details are not included. [C13] [C14]

Source hashes, derived tables, calculation scripts, report sources and validation receipts accompany this publication. Third-party full articles/supplements and private working documents are not redistributed. Historical reports are retained as dated records; this revision is the current interpretation. The Monash finding is an attributed scientific paraphrase. The original correspondence, attachment and contact details are not reproduced; the public conference abstract supplies assay context, while the personal communication supplies the G359E result. [SM12] [SM14]

The complete baseline trial RNA analysis used all 28 available samples and fixed endpoints, memberships and tests. Independent reconstruction reproduced every gene-level TPM column, all 24 scoring/endpoint result rows and 72 exact tests; all 21 frozen scientific sources matched their hashes. Public aggregate outputs and portable code document full reproduction requirements without redistributing raw FASTQs, subject-labelled clinical matrices or third-party supplements. [VR1] [VR2]

Only attributed, minimal vaccine/access paraphrases are included. No original private emails, QC workbook, consultation transcript, contact details, costs or full copyrighted review are redistributed. Earlier numerical case/trial sources remain pinned; the five new leads do not alter the four-programme q=.521 result. [VE9] [VR1]
